WAL-CLM-RARE-000330.question: Where does the word zinc come from?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000330.answer_short: Wallach recounts that Erasmus Ebener was credited as the first to recognize metallic zinc around 1509, and that the physician Paracelsus named the new metal 'zinken.'

WAL-CLM-RARE-000331.subject: magnesium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000331.question: Is magnesium what makes plants green?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000331.answer_short: Yes — magnesium sits at the center of the chlorophyll molecule, which is exactly why green plants (and lush places like Hawaiian rain forests) are so green.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000332.subject: magnesium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000332.question: Is magnesium used to treat seizures?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000332.answer_short: Yes — magnesium has a long medical record as an anticonvulsant and anesthetic; intravenous magnesium sulfate has been used since 1925 to control eclampsia, the convulsions of pregnancy.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000333.subject: magnesium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000333.question: Where do Epsom salts come from?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000333.answer_short: Epsom salt is magnesium sulfate, first discovered in a bitter mineral spring near the English village of Epsom during the drought of 1618.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000268.subject: zinc
WAL-CLM-RARE-000268.question: Do athletes need more zinc?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000268.answer_short: Yes — Wallach notes that heavy zinc losses occur in sweat, so unsupplemented athletes are especially prone to zinc deficiency.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000141.subject: zinc
WAL-CLM-LETS-000141.question: Why can't I smell anything anymore?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000141.answer_short: Wallach says a chronic loss of the sense of smell is the result of a zinc deficiency, and zinc at 50 mg three times a day is very effective at bringing smell back.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000276.subject: zinc
WAL-CLM-LETS-000276.question: What do white spots on my fingernails mean?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000276.answer_short: In Wallach's framework, white spots on the fingernails are a sign of zinc deficiency, with the nails acting as a visible barometer of your nutritional status.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000040.subject: zinc
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000040.question: What blocks zinc absorption?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000040.answer_short: Wallach warns that too much dietary copper and iron, plus high-phytate vegan diets, all cut down how much zinc the body can actually take up.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000166.subject: zinc
WAL-CLM-LETS-000166.question: Does zinc help with body odor?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000166.answer_short: Wallach treats body odor and foot odor — in anyone, but especially teenagers and older people — with zinc at 50 mg three times a day.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000157.subject: zinc
WAL-CLM-LETS-000157.question: Does zinc help an enlarged prostate?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000157.answer_short: Yes — Wallach treats benign prostatic hypertrophy (an enlarged prostate) with zinc at 50 mg three times a day, alongside flaxseed oil, saw palmetto, vitamin A and other supports.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000086.subject: zinc
WAL-CLM-RARE-000086.question: Does smoking affect my zinc?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000086.answer_short: Wallach explains that cadmium — about 23 micrograms per pack of cigarettes and a major part of second-hand smoke — interferes with zinc.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000210.subject: zinc
WAL-CLM-LETS-000210.question: What causes cerebral palsy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000210.answer_short: Wallach holds that cerebral palsy is a birth defect of the cerebellum caused by a preconception deficiency of zinc and vitamin B-6 in the mother — and once it forms there is no treatment.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000365.subject: zinc
WAL-CLM-LETS-000365.question: Can a zinc deficiency cause a miscarriage?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000365.answer_short: Wallach holds that zinc is one of the nutrients essential to maintaining a pregnancy, and that deficiencies of it (along with vitamin A, folic acid, selenium and protein) are a common cause of miscarriage.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000044.subject: zinc
WAL-CLM-RARE-000044.question: Is Down's syndrome really genetic?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000044.answer_short: Wallach's provocative stance is that Down's syndrome is not genetic at all but the result of a preconception zinc deficiency that produces chromosome damage.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000010.subject: zinc
WAL-CLM-RARE-000010.question: What does Wallach say causes cystic fibrosis?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000010.answer_short: Wallach argues cystic fibrosis is largely an acquired environmental disease driven by a deficiency of selenium, zinc, and riboflavin, made worse by low vitamin E and diets rich in polyunsaturated fats.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000207.subject: magnesium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000207.question: What does magnesium actually do in the body?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000207.answer_short: In Wallach's framework magnesium is required to produce and transfer energy, build proteins, contract your muscles, and fire your nerves — while too much of it can actually inhibit bone from calcifying.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000208.subject: magnesium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000208.question: Why is magnesium called the source of all biological energy?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000208.answer_short: Wallach points out that magnesium is the metal atom at the heart of chlorophyll in every green plant — making it, in his words, the ultimate source of all biological energy.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000016.subject: magnesium
WAL-CLM-LETS-000016.question: What are the signs I'm low on magnesium?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000016.answer_short: Wallach lists the signs of magnesium deficiency as anxiety, confusion, irritability and restlessness, depression, and even birth defects.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000074.subject: magnesium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000074.question: Why do I keep getting muscle cramps and charley horses?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000074.answer_short: Wallach calls a muscle cramp a 'mini-convulsion' in the muscle, caused by deficiencies of calcium, magnesium, potassium, and selenium.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000174.subject: magnesium
WAL-CLM-LETS-000174.question: Why do I grind my teeth at night?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000174.answer_short: Wallach lists teeth grinding (bruxism) as a possible sign of a magnesium, calcium, or B-6 deficiency — along with food allergies and low blood sugar.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000082.subject: magnesium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000082.question: What does high magnesium on a hair analysis mean?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000082.answer_short: Counterintuitively, elevated calcium and magnesium on a hair test can signal depletion — minerals being shed from the bones — revealing active osteoporosis, arthritis, gum disease, and a tendency toward kidney stones.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000209.subject: magnesium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000209.question: What's the most absorbable form of magnesium?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000209.answer_short: Wallach says magnesium absorption ranges from just 24% up to 85% — metallic (rock/mineral) forms are absorbed the least, while plant-derived magnesium is absorbed the best.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000056.subject: magnesium
WAL-CLM-LETS-000056.question: How much magnesium should I take a day?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000056.answer_short: In his Base Line Nutritional Supplement Program Wallach gives magnesium a daily maintenance need (True Supplement Need) of 1,000 mg, with a 30-day pharmacologic dose also of 1,000 mg — well above the government RDA of 350 mg, which he reprints only to argue against.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000060.subject: magnesium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000060.question: How much magnesium does Wallach recommend a day?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000060.answer_short: Wallach's standard pairing is calcium at 2,000 mg and magnesium at 1,000 mg a day — a two-to-one combination he prescribes for osteoporosis and other bone and mineral problems.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000098.subject: magnesium
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000098.question: What are the symptoms of magnesium deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000098.answer_short: Wallach ties a long list of problems to magnesium shortage — including asthma, menstrual migraines, depression, tetany and convulsions, tremors, muscular weakness, vertigo, ECG changes, and abnormal calcification of arteries and soft tissue.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000205.subject: magnesium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000205.question: Is cholesterol really what hardens your arteries?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000205.answer_short: No — Wallach argues the real driver of arterial hardening is magnesium deficiency, not cholesterol; a lack of magnesium lets calcium deposit into the artery walls in what he calls 'malignant calcification.'

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000157.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000157.question: What do essential fatty acids do in the body?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000157.answer_short: Wallach says EFAs have vitamin-like roles in fat transport and metabolism and in keeping cell walls (the bilipid membranes) intact, and they form part of the cholesterol esters and phospholipids in the blood.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000158.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000158.question: Is eczema related to omega-3 or essential fatty acids?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000158.answer_short: Wallach says atopic dermatitis (eczema) is part of the 'atopic' syndrome — which also includes asthma, hair loss and lowered immunity — and is a condition of essential fatty acid malabsorption.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000159.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000159.question: Why is the cystic fibrosis sweat test positive?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000159.answer_short: Wallach says the positive CF 'sweat test' results from essential fatty acid deficiency, which causes a secondary shortage of prostaglandins that control the sodium, chloride and potassium levels of sweat.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000160.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000160.question: Does an omega-3 or essential fatty acid deficiency cause acne?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000160.answer_short: Wallach says acne is primarily the result of an essential fatty acid deficiency combined with eating too much saturated and polyunsaturated fat from fried foods and margarine.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000161.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000161.question: What are the best sources of omega-3 or essential fatty acids?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000161.answer_short: Wallach points to flaxseed oil and salmon oil as the essential fats to take, and advises avoiding as much of the other polyunsaturated fats as possible.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000162.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000162.question: Is dry skin a sign of omega-3 or essential fatty acid deficiency?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000162.answer_short: Yes — Wallach says dry skin, cracked cuticles and hangnails signal essential fatty acid deficiency that can lead to cardiovascular disease; he sums it up as 'dry skin means essential fatty acids.'

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000163.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000163.question: How much vitamin C should I take?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000163.answer_short: For treating abrasions, Wallach recommends taking vitamin C orally to bowel tolerance — anywhere from 1 to 5 grams.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000164.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000164.question: Should people with MS avoid vitamin C supplements?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000164.answer_short: For multiple sclerosis (and ALS), Wallach advises avoiding large-dose vitamin C supplements and getting vitamin C from green vegetables and juices instead.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000165.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000165.question: What causes night blindness?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000165.answer_short: Wallach says night blindness is caused by a vitamin A deficiency, from a poor diet, fat malabsorption, or a zinc shortage that blocks the liver from converting carotene to vitamin A.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000166.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000166.question: Why do I have rough bumpy skin on my arms?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000166.answer_short: Wallach says rough, sandpaper-like 'shark skin' (keratosis) is caused by a deficiency of vitamin A and zinc, often from a low-animal-protein diet.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000167.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000167.question: How does Wallach use vitamin A to fight cancer?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000167.answer_short: Wallach says beta-carotene with vitamin E can be taken at up to 600,000 IU of vitamin A equivalent in cancer therapy, helping the thymus make antibodies and making laetrile more effective.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000168.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000168.question: How does Wallach treat acne with vitamin A?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000168.answer_short: Wallach recommends vitamin A at 300,000 units a day as beta-carotene for five months, then dropping to 25,000 a day, along with B6, zinc, and topical vitamin E oil.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000169.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000169.question: What is keratomalacia?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000169.answer_short: Keratomalacia is a severe vitamin A deficiency disease in which the cornea turns hazy, dry, and ulcerated, and if untreated it can cause permanent blindness.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000170.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000170.question: Can vitamin A deficiency cause miscarriage or birth defects?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000170.answer_short: Wallach says miscarriage is usually due to deficiencies of vitamins, trace minerals, or protein, and names vitamin A, zinc, folic acid, selenium, and complete proteins as essential to maintaining a pregnancy.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000171.subject: vitamin-d
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000171.question: How much vitamin D should an adult take?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000171.answer_short: Wallach advises adults to avoid vitamin D, warning that more than 400 IU a day results in calcification of the coronary arteries.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000172.subject: vitamin-d
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000172.question: How do you treat rickets with vitamin D?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000172.answer_short: Wallach treats rickets — a vitamin D deficiency disease — with vitamin D at 400 IU orally twice a day, plus calcium and magnesium and 30 minutes of daily sunshine.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000173.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000173.question: Is iron storage disease really an iron problem?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000173.answer_short: No, Wallach lists iron storage disease and iron-resistant anemia as symptoms of copper deficiency, not of iron itself.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000174.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000174.question: What is calcium?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000174.answer_short: Calcium is the fifth most abundant mineral in the earth's crust and the most abundant mineral in the human body — the structural mineral of bones and teeth that also powers muscle contraction, blood clotting, nerve signaling and the heartbeat.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000175.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000175.question: What causes calcium deficiency or blocks calcium absorption?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000175.answer_short: Low vitamin D, low stomach acid, lactose intolerance, celiac disease, high-fat or low-protein diets, and phytates all reduce the calcium the body can absorb.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000176.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000176.question: Why can't my body hold onto the calcium I take?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000176.answer_short: Without the gelatinous bone matrix (collagen/gelatin), most supplemental calcium can't be retained in bone and is simply urinated out.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000177.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000177.question: How do calcium and magnesium work together?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000177.answer_short: Calcium and magnesium have opposite roles — calcium stimulates muscle contraction while magnesium relaxes it — so the two need to stay in balance.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000178.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000178.question: Do you need dairy to get enough calcium?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000178.answer_short: No — Wallach notes the Chinese eat no dairy yet get their calcium from animal bones, often simmered in vinegar to leach the minerals into soup.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000179.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000179.question: Can you get enough calcium from food alone?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000179.answer_short: No — Wallach says American diets are critically deficient in calcium and the only practical way to get enough is through supplementation.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000180.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000180.question: What is the ideal calcium to phosphorus ratio?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000180.answer_short: Wallach says the ideal dietary calcium-to-phosphorus ratio is 2:1, which is impossible to hit from food alone because the American diet is loaded with phosphorus.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000181.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000181.question: How much calcium did our ancestors eat compared to people today?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000181.answer_short: Stone Age humans got 1,600–3,000 mg of calcium a day, while 20th-century Americans get only one-fifth to one-third that — roughly 300–680 mg.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000182.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000182.question: How did Wallach first discover that calcium fixed his own health problem?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000182.answer_short: At age 14, after library books tied his eyelid cramps and twitches to calcium deficiency, Wallach ate calcium-loaded calf pellets and the twitches went away in four days.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000197.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000197.question: What is Omega-3?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000197.answer_short: Omega-3 is one of the two fatty acids Wallach classes as truly essential — alpha-linolenic acid — a fat the body cannot make and must get from food.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000198.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000198.question: Can omega-3 help with depression?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000198.answer_short: Low DHA (an omega-3) tracks with low brain 5-HIAA, which Wallach links to higher rates of depression and suicide.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000199.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000199.question: Does omega-3 slow aging?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000199.answer_short: Wallach cites research in which omega-3 supplementation lengthened DNA telomeres and lowered inflammation in obese adults.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000200.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000200.question: Can low omega-3 cause blood clots or a heart attack?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000200.answer_short: Yes — Wallach lists coronary thrombosis as a disease caused by omega-3 deficiency, not by genetics.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000201.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000201.question: What does omega-3 do in the body?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000201.answer_short: Essential fatty acids like omega-3 are the raw material for prostaglandins that regulate blood pressure, heart rate, blood clotting, airway opening, and brain neurotransmitters.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000202.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000202.question: What is the ideal ratio of omega-3 to omega-6?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000202.answer_short: Wallach points out that traditional diets contained nearly equal amounts of omega-3 and omega-6 essential fatty acids.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000203.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000203.question: Why did Wallach take the FDA to court over omega-3?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000203.answer_short: Wallach was plaintiff in eight FDA lawsuits — up to the Supreme Court steps — to make information on omega-3, selenium, folic acid and antioxidants available to Americans.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000204.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000204.question: Why is it called omega-3?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000204.answer_short: The '3' marks where the first double bond sits — three carbons in from the tail (methyl) end of the fatty acid.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000205.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000205.question: What is Vitamin C?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000205.answer_short: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is a water-soluble antioxidant that most mammals make in their own bodies, but humans cannot -- so we must get it from food or supplements every day.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000206.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000206.question: What does vitamin C do in the body?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000206.answer_short: Vitamin C is a required cofactor for building collagen, connective tissue, cartilage, bones, teeth and blood vessels, and it improves iron absorption.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000207.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000207.question: Does vitamin C help the immune system?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000207.answer_short: Yes — vitamin C affects white blood cells, macrophages, immune responses, wound healing and allergic reactions.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000208.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000208.question: Can your body store vitamin C?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000208.answer_short: No — humans cannot store vitamin C, so it must be replenished from the diet every day.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000209.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000209.question: Can you take too much vitamin C?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000209.answer_short: Yes — too much vitamin C can cause oxalate crystal deposits, urinary tract inflammation, diarrhea, and breakdown of red blood cells.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000210.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000210.question: Who discovered the cure for scurvy?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000210.answer_short: Scottish naval surgeon James Lind proved in 1753 that lemons and oranges cured scurvy, in one of the first controlled experiments.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000211.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000211.question: Who made vitamin C famous?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000211.answer_short: Linus Pauling — his 1970 book 'Vitamin C and the Common Cold' triggered a national surge in vitamin C use dubbed the 'Linus Pauling effect.'

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000212.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000212.question: Why is vitamin C called ascorbic acid?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000212.answer_short: It was named 'ascorbic' — meaning 'without scurvy' — after Szent-Gyorgyi first jokingly proposed calling it 'ignosco' and 'godnose.'

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000213.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000213.question: What is Vitamin A?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000213.answer_short: Vitamin A is a fat-soluble vitamin, isolated in 1913, that exists in several active forms — retinol, retinoic acid, and retinyl esters — and is essential for vision, healthy skin and mucous membranes, and strong bones and teeth.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000214.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000214.question: What is vitamin A?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000214.answer_short: Vitamin A is a fat-soluble vitamin, isolated in 1913, that exists in several active forms and is essential for vision, skin, mucous membranes, bones, and teeth.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000215.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000215.question: What does vitamin A do in the body?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000215.answer_short: Vitamin A drives growth, maintains epithelial tissues like the retina, gut lining, and skin, and helps make adrenal steroid hormones.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000216.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000216.question: Can you absorb vitamin A on a low-fat diet?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000216.answer_short: Wallach says no, vitamin A is fat-soluble and is poorly absorbed on low-fat diets, and people without a gallbladder should take ox bile to absorb it.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000217.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000217.question: Can you take too much vitamin A?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000217.answer_short: Yes, sustained high intakes of retinol can be toxic, but Wallach says overdose signs generally appear only above about 50,000 IU of retinol a day in adults.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000218.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000218.question: How was vitamin A discovered?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000218.answer_short: Vitamin A was discovered in 1913 when two research groups found that animals fed only lard developed a deficiency that was corrected by adding butter, egg yolk, and cod liver oil.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000219.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000219.question: Was cystic fibrosis first thought to be a vitamin A deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000219.answer_short: Yes, Wallach notes that when cystic fibrosis was first described in 1933 it was thought to be a vitamin A deficiency, based on vitamin A deficiency changes seen in young celiac patients.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000220.subject: vitamin-d
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000220.question: What is Vitamin D?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000220.answer_short: Vitamin D is a fat-soluble vitamin with two forms — D2 from plants and D3, which the body makes when sunlight converts cholesterol in the skin — and it is essential for depositing calcium and phosphorus in the bones and teeth.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000221.subject: vitamin-d
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000221.question: Why is vitamin D deficiency so common today?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000221.answer_short: Wallach calls the universal vitamin D deficiency of the 20th and 21st centuries a physician-caused disease driven by medical advice to avoid the sun and skip cholesterol and supplements.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000222.subject: vitamin-d
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000222.question: Is vitamin D a hormone?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000222.answer_short: Wallach notes some consider vitamin D a hormone, since it is synthesized in one place, like the skin, and acts on a distant target, like bone, much like steroid hormones.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000223.subject: vitamin-d
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000223.question: How was vitamin D discovered to cure rickets?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000223.answer_short: Early 20th-century researchers proved both sunlight and diet cured rickets — Hulschinsky straightened deformed limbs with UV lamps, and Mellanby and McCollum showed cod liver oil cured it even after its vitamin A was destroyed.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000224.subject: vitamin-d
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000224.question: Is rickets making a comeback?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000224.answer_short: Yes — Wallach reports rickets reappeared in the industrialized world in 2013 with a 400 percent increase between 1995 and 2011, which he blames on sun-avoidance, sunscreen, and fear of cholesterol.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000225.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000225.question: What is iron?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000225.answer_short: Iron is an essential mineral found in nearly every living thing; in the body it sits at the heart of hemoglobin, the protein that carries oxygen in the blood, and a healthy adult holds about 3 to 5 grams of it.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000226.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000226.question: What is iron and what does it do in the body?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000226.answer_short: Iron is an essential element in nearly all living things; a healthy adult carries 3 to 5 grams of it, mostly in hemoglobin and other oxygen-handling proteins.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000227.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000227.question: What causes iron deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000227.answer_short: Iron deficiency comes from unsupplemented pregnancy, menstruation, chronic infections, low stomach acid, chronic diarrhea or bleeding, and impaired absorption from high-fat, high-phytate, or gluten-intolerant diets.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000228.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000228.question: Is too much iron dangerous?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000228.answer_short: Wallach argues iron overload is falsely blamed for diseases like cirrhosis and diabetes; excess stored iron is actually caused by shortages of selenium, copper, and zinc.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000229.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000229.question: If I have iron-deficiency anemia, do I have other deficiencies too?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000229.answer_short: Almost certainly, Wallach says deficiencies rarely occur alone, so an obvious one like iron-deficiency anemia usually means others, maybe dozens, are present.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000230.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000230.question: Can iron actually cure pica or ice-eating?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000230.answer_short: Yes, Wallach cites trials where iron cured children of eating sand and made ice-eating disappear once the underlying anemia was corrected.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000231.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000231.question: Why did ancient people call iron the metal from the sky?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000231.answer_short: Because the first purified iron came from meteors, the Egyptians called iron 'the metal from the sky' and the Aztecs 'the gift of heaven.'

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000232.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000232.question: How much calcium is in the human body and where is it stored?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000232.answer_short: Calcium is the most abundant mineral in the body—about 1,200 g in men and 1,000 g in women—with 99 percent of it stored in the bones and teeth.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000233.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000233.question: What does calcium do in the body besides build bones?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000233.answer_short: Beyond bone structure, calcium is required for muscle contraction, blood clotting, nerve transmission, hormone secretion, and regulating the heartbeat.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000234.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000234.question: Does calcium need vitamin D to be absorbed?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000234.answer_short: Yes—Wallach says vitamin D is required for the absorption, metabolism, and proper deposition of calcium (and phosphorus) in the bones and teeth.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000235.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000235.question: Can bone spurs and calcium deposits be reversed?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000235.answer_short: Yes—Wallach says bone spurs, heel spurs, and calcium deposits form during raging osteoporosis and can be reversed and eliminated by supplementing with significant amounts of chelated and colloidal calcium.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000236.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000236.question: How did Wallach discover that kidney stones come from too little calcium?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000236.answer_short: In zoo tortoises and iguanas fed diets with no added calcium, Wallach found the calcium in their kidney stones had been leached from their own bones and shells during raging osteoporosis—proof stones come from too little calcium, not too much.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000020.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000020.question: Which nuts have the most omega-3?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000020.answer_short: Walnuts — Wallach says English walnuts are the only nut with significant levels of omega-3 fatty acids.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000021.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000021.question: Does low omega-3 raise cholesterol or cause obesity?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000021.answer_short: Wallach ties omega-3 deficiency to elevated total cholesterol and LDL, obesity, peripheral neuropathies, thrombotic disease, and atherosclerosis.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000022.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000022.question: Does omega-3 help prevent dementia or Alzheimer's?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000022.answer_short: Wallach cites a Framingham/Tufts study in which diets rich in omega-3 cut the risk of new dementia by 48 percent.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000023.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000023.question: How much vitamin C did Linus Pauling recommend?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000023.answer_short: Linus Pauling recommended taking 10 to 12 grams of vitamin C every day - for colds, and to help prevent cancer and heart disease.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000024.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000024.question: What foods are high in vitamin C?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000024.answer_short: Wallach notes that capsicum - cayenne peppers - are rich in vitamin C.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000025.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000025.question: Can vitamin C help prevent Alzheimer's disease?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000025.answer_short: In a Johns Hopkins study, people taking vitamin C and vitamin E had a 78% lower risk of Alzheimer's disease.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000026.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000026.question: Does vitamin C prevent cancer?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000026.answer_short: In a large five-year National Cancer Institute study, vitamin C showed no statistically significant protective effect on cancer deaths.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000027.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000027.question: Is synthetic vitamin C the same as natural vitamin C?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000027.answer_short: Wallach recounts that when vitamin C was first synthesized in 1933, the artificial form was identical to the natural one.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000028.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000028.question: How did vitamin A get its name, and how is it related to vitamin D?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000028.answer_short: Wallach recounts that in 1922 the original 'vitamin A' was found to consist of two separate factors: the growth factor kept the name vitamin A, while the anti-rachitic (anti-rickets) factor was designated vitamin D.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000029.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000029.question: Can iron deficiency make you fat?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000029.answer_short: Wallach says a combined iron and phosphorus deficiency can trigger almost psychotic binge eating and soft-drink bingeing that ends in morbid obesity.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000030.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000030.question: Does calcium help with weight loss?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000030.answer_short: Wallach says consuming 1,200 mg of calcium a day cuts your risk of being overweight by 65 percent, and combined with dropping 500 calories a day it doubles the rate of weight loss—without exercise.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000277.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000277.question: How much omega-3 do I need each day?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000277.answer_short: Wallach sets the daily essential fatty acid requirement at two to three percent of calories — about five grams on a 1,500-calorie diet.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000278.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000278.question: How can I absorb omega-3 if my gallbladder was removed?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000278.answer_short: Wallach advises supplementing ox bile after gallbladder removal so bile salts can absorb essential fatty acids and other good fats.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000279.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000279.question: Can omega-3 prevent stroke and sudden heart death?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000279.answer_short: Wallach says supplementing omega-3 essential fatty acids reduces the risk of stroke and coronary-thrombosis sudden death — a claim the FDA long forbade sharing.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000280.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000280.question: Does vitamin C help with colds?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000280.answer_short: Vitamin C has been shown to cut the rate, severity and duration of a cold by about 20% on average.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000281.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000281.question: Do smokers need more vitamin C?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000281.answer_short: Yes - cigarette smoking roughly doubles the body's need for vitamin C.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000282.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000282.question: Who discovered vitamin C and when was it isolated?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000282.answer_short: Pure ascorbic acid was isolated in 1928 by Albert Szent-Gyorgyi; in 1932 C. Glenn King reisolated it from lemons and identified it as vitamin C.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000283.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000283.question: Why were British sailors called limeys?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000283.answer_short: British sailors were nicknamed 'limeys' because they carried lemons on their ships to prevent and cure scurvy.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000284.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000284.question: Why can't I absorb vitamin A even when I eat enough?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000284.answer_short: Vitamin A is fat-soluble, so it is absorbed with dietary fats — anything that blocks fat absorption (antibiotics, gallbladder disease, celiac disease, high-fiber diets, mineral oil) blocks vitamin A too.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000285.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000285.question: What foods are highest in vitamin A?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000285.answer_short: Beef liver is by far the richest source, followed by carrots, sweet potato, spinach, and dried apricots; plants carry vitamin A as carotenoids in yellow, red, and orange pigments.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000286.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000286.question: How did they figure out vitamin A cures eye disease?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000286.answer_short: Animals on fat-free diets developed eye inflammation and infections that reversed with butter or cod liver oil, and in 1924 Bloch showed childhood xerophthalmia was the same disease.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000287.subject: vitamin-d
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000287.question: What does vitamin D do in the body?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000287.answer_short: Vitamin D drives intestinal absorption of calcium and phosphate and, with parathyroid hormone, mobilizes calcium from bone to keep blood levels normal; it also mobilizes phosphate from bone and helps the kidney reabsorb calcium from urine.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000288.subject: vitamin-d
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000288.question: How does the body make vitamin D from sunlight?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000288.answer_short: In the skin, sunlight or UV light drives the conversion of cholesterol into 7-dehydrocholesterol, the provitamin of vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol); UV light also converts the yeast sterol ergosterol into vitamin D2.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000289.subject: vitamin-d
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000289.question: Can vitamin D prevent cancer and chronic disease?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000289.answer_short: Wallach cites research that vitamin D deficiency raises the risk of heart attacks, breast and colon cancer mortality, and childhood type II diabetes, while adequate vitamin D may help prevent many serious chronic diseases.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000290.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000290.question: Is iron from plants as good as iron from meat?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000290.answer_short: No — heme iron from meat is 10% absorbable, while iron from fresh plants is only 1% absorbable because of the plant's phytates.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000291.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000291.question: How is calcium absorbed in the body?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000291.answer_short: Calcium is absorbed mainly in the acidic duodenum, and absorption drops as the gut turns alkaline; metallic forms may yield only 1-3%, while colloidal or chelated forms reach up to 98%.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000292.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000292.question: Why doesn't calcium carbonate work well as a supplement?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000292.answer_short: Calcium carbonate is a metallic mineral that is barely absorbed — you'd have to take about 25 capsules a day to actually net 2,000 mg of usable calcium.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000293.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000293.question: Where does the word calcium come from and who discovered it?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000293.answer_short: The name comes from the Latin 'calx' (lime), used by the Romans in the 1st century, and the metal was isolated in 1808 by Sir Humphry Davy.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000497.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-LETS-000497.question: Can omega-3 / essential fatty acids help cystic fibrosis?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000497.answer_short: Wallach says cystic fibrosis is prevented in animals by adequate selenium and essential fatty acid nutrition in the mother, and treated in people with flaxseed oil and selenium.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000498.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-LETS-000498.question: Does omega-3 help with PMS?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000498.answer_short: Wallach says PMS is driven by essential fatty acid deficiency acting with the monthly hormone cycle, and he includes EFAs in his PMS treatment.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000499.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-LETS-000499.question: Can vitamin C deficiency cause nosebleeds?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000499.answer_short: Wallach says nosebleeds are usually the result of vitamin K and/or vitamin C deficiencies.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000500.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-LETS-000500.question: How much vitamin C should I take when I'm sick?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000500.answer_short: Wallach recommends taking vitamin C 'to bowel tolerance' - and, if you already have diarrhea, 1,000 mg time-release tablets hourly through the day.
topics: how much vitamin c when sick

WAL-CLM-LETS-000501.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-LETS-000501.question: Is cervical dysplasia caused by vitamin A deficiency?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000501.answer_short: Wallach considers cervical dysplasia a manifestation of chronic vitamin A deficiency and treats it with Lugol's iodine plus beta carotene and zinc.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000502.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-LETS-000502.question: Can low vitamin A cause infertility?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000502.answer_short: Wallach describes a woman whose infertility traced to a blood vitamin A level at 10% of normal from malabsorption, who conceived once it was corrected.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000503.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-LETS-000503.question: What does iron deficiency look like on a blood test?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000503.answer_short: Iron deficiency shows up as decreased hemoglobin and small red cells — the picture of a microcytic anemia.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000504.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-LETS-000504.question: How much iron should I take for heavy periods?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000504.answer_short: Wallach's protocol for painful or heavy periods includes 25 to 50 mg of iron a day, especially for vegetarian women who do not eat red meat or liver regularly.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000505.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-LETS-000505.question: Is arthritis caused by a calcium deficiency?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000505.answer_short: Wallach holds that arthritis is fundamentally a calcium deficiency made worse by too much phosphorus in the American diet.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000334.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-RARE-000334.question: Can a hair analysis reveal an essential fatty acid deficiency?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000334.answer_short: Yes — Wallach says high hair sodium, potassium, and chloride signal an EFA deficiency, because the skin glands lose electrolytes instead of conserving them.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000335.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-RARE-000335.question: What's the best way to get beta carotene naturally?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000335.answer_short: Wallach says juicing is one of the greatest ways he knows to get fresh, natural beta carotene, though it can't supply the full spectrum of essential minerals.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000336.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-RARE-000336.question: Is there evidence that beta carotene helps prevent cancer?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000336.answer_short: Rare Earths reproduces a newspaper report of a National Cancer Institute trial in a rural area of China where beta carotene with vitamin E and selenium dramatically cut cancer deaths — called the first hard evidence antioxidants protect against cancer.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000337.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-RARE-000337.question: Why do redheads have red hair?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000337.answer_short: Red hair gets its color from an iron-containing pigment, so redheads have relatively high iron in their hair.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000338.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-RARE-000338.question: Is the iron in cheap supplements just rust?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000338.answer_short: Often yes—metallic forms like iron oxide are literally rust and only 8 to 12 percent absorbable, dropping to 3 to 5 percent after age 35–40.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000339.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-RARE-000339.question: What is the story of the iron baby?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000339.answer_short: In 1850 a woman who had lost three pregnancies took iron scales from a blacksmith's anvil steeped in cider through her next pregnancy and delivered a boy so strong he walked at nine months—the 'iron baby.'

WAL-CLM-RARE-000340.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000340.question: Why do children eat dirt or paint chips?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000340.answer_short: Wallach attributes pica -- the craving to eat non-food items -- to mineral deficiency: calcium-deficient rats will drink large amounts of a bad-tasting lead acetate solution, unlike calcium-fed controls.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000341.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000341.question: Does an all-meat carnivore diet cause calcium deficiency?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000341.answer_short: Yes — Wallach says even an organ-meat-rich carnivore diet still lacks enough calcium, magnesium and manganese, producing the classic degenerative diseases of pure carnivores.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000342.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000342.question: Has calcium been used as medicine throughout history?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000342.answer_short: Yes—calcium was used for infantile convulsions as far back as 1689, and rickets was linked to calcium deficiency as early as 850 B.C.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000063.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000063.question: Which fatty acids does Wallach say are actually essential?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000063.answer_short: Of the three EFAs — linoleic, linolenic, and arachidonic — only linoleic and linolenic are truly essential, since the body can make arachidonic acid from linolenic.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000053.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000053.question: Why do babies and children need omega-3?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000053.answer_short: Wallach warns that EFA deficiency in infants causes poor growth, lowered IQ, seizures, learning disabilities, eczema, asthma, and weaker immunity.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000115.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000115.question: How much omega-3 or essential fatty acids should I take per day?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000115.answer_short: Wallach says essential fatty acids should make up 3 percent of your total daily calories, or be supplemented at 9 grams per day in capsule form.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000283.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-RARE-000283.question: Can omega-3 replace blood thinners or blood pressure drugs?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000283.answer_short: In Wallach's drug-replacement guide, omega-3 oils are listed among the nutrients that stand in for blood thinners and blood pressure drugs.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000011.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-LETS-000011.question: What are the signs of essential fatty acid deficiency?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000011.answer_short: Wallach lists acne, hair loss, eczema, brittle hair, arthritis, gallstones, impaired wound healing, infertility and more as signs of essential fatty acid deficiency.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000055.subject: omega-3
WAL-CLM-RARE-000055.question: Are omega-3s one of the essential nutrients the body needs?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000055.answer_short: Yes — Wallach counts three essential fatty acids among the 90 nutrients the body requires, including for immune defense.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000428.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-LETS-000428.question: What causes scurvy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000428.answer_short: Wallach identifies scurvy, marked by bleeding gums, as a disease caused by vitamin C deficiency.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000117.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000117.question: How much vitamin C should I take a day?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000117.answer_short: Wallach's daily multiple recommends 250 to 1,000 mg of vitamin C (ascorbic acid) for adults and children over 9.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000417.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-LETS-000417.question: Can vitamin C be given intravenously?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000417.answer_short: Yes, for Reye's syndrome Wallach uses intravenous vitamin C at 5-10 grams per day.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000043.subject: vitamin-c
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000043.question: What are the signs of vitamin C deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000043.answer_short: Vitamin C deficiency can cause bleeding gums, loose teeth, bruising, dry rough skin, poor growth, slow wound healing, elevated cancer risk and scurvy.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000031.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000031.question: What are the signs of vitamin A deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000031.answer_short: Vitamin A deficiency shows up as night blindness and other eye problems, dry and bumpy skin, acne, infertility, birth defects, depression, weak immunity, poor growth, bone disease, and higher cancer risk.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000110.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000110.question: How much vitamin A should I take daily?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000110.answer_short: Wallach's daily multiple recommends about 2,500 to 5,000 IU of vitamin A as retinol plus 5,000 to 25,000 IU as beta-carotene for adults and children over nine.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000037.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-LETS-000037.question: What are the signs of too much vitamin A?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000037.answer_short: Vitamin A toxicity causes abdominal pain, hair loss, missed periods, cracked lips, GI upset, enlarged liver and spleen, joint pain, nausea, itching, and weight loss.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000056.subject: vitamin-a
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000056.question: Can you overdose on beta-carotene?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000056.answer_short: Wallach says it is almost impossible to overdose on beta-carotene, the first sign being dry skin, and he uses it at a vitamin A equivalent of about 300,000 IU per day.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000032.subject: vitamin-d
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000032.question: What are the symptoms of vitamin D deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000032.answer_short: Vitamin D deficiency can cause facial tics, muscle cramps, tetany and convulsions, childhood rickets, osteoporosis, arthritis, kidney stones, and more.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000083.subject: vitamin-d
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000083.question: Can too much vitamin D be dangerous?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000083.answer_short: Yes — Wallach teaches that vitamin D toxicity is angiotoxic, targeting the elastic arteries and causing fibrosis of arterial smooth muscle and calcification of blood vessel walls.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000126.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000126.question: Why does the body need iron?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000126.answer_short: Iron sits at the center of hemoglobin, where its atoms bind oxygen in the lungs and carry it to every cell.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000131.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000131.question: What are the symptoms of iron deficiency?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000131.answer_short: Iron deficiency brings fatigue, listlessness, palpitations on exertion, poor memory and concentration, a sore tongue, and microcytic anemia.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000130.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-RARE-000130.question: What does iron do in the body?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000130.answer_short: Iron builds hemoglobin and myoglobin and transfers electrons so the body can use oxygen—'iron is to hemoglobin what magnesium is to chlorophyll.'

WAL-CLM-LETS-000054.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-LETS-000054.question: How much iron should you take a day?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000054.answer_short: Wallach's baseline adult program lists 45 mg of iron a day — well above the 18 mg RDA — with a therapeutic range of 50 to 100 mg.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000133.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000133.question: Can you get too much iron?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000133.answer_short: Yes — excess iron can lead to liver cirrhosis, pancreatic fibrosis, diabetes and heart failure, largely by driving up the body's need for other minerals.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000129.subject: iron
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000129.question: Is eating ice or dirt a sign of iron deficiency?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000129.answer_short: Yes — Wallach says pica (craving ice, dirt, paint, or excess food) is a specific sign of iron deficiency.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000079.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-LETS-000079.question: Can a blood test detect calcium deficiency?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000079.answer_short: No — Wallach says your blood calcium stays in the normal range even during a raging calcium deficiency, so a standard blood test misses it.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000004.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-LETS-000004.question: What are the symptoms of calcium deficiency?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000004.answer_short: Signs range from arthritis, bone spurs, osteoporosis and tooth decay to muscle cramps, insomnia, depression, hypertension and pica.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000045.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-LETS-000045.question: How much calcium should an adult take daily?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000045.answer_short: Wallach's baseline program sets a true daily need of 2,000 mg of calcium, with a therapeutic range of 2,000 to 5,000 mg — far above the 800 mg RDA.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000071.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000071.question: Can calcium deficiency cause high blood pressure?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000071.answer_short: Yes — Wallach cites research linking chronic calcium deficiency to hypertension, with more than 30 studies supporting it and lower ionized calcium found in untreated hypertensives.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000059.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000059.question: Can osteoporosis be cured?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000059.answer_short: Wallach says osteoporosis is easy to prevent and cure with proper supplementation of stomach acid (HCl) and calcium—estrogen and fluoride alone don't solve it.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000009.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000009.question: What diseases can calcium deficiency cause?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000009.answer_short: Wallach ties calcium deficiency to as many as 147 different diseases, from osteoporosis and arthritis to Bell's palsy, tinnitus, and trigeminal neuralgia.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000087.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000087.question: Does taking calcium cause kidney stones?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000087.answer_short: No — Wallach says kidney and bladder stones are ironically caused by calcium and magnesium deficiency, with the stone minerals coming from your own bones.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000073.subject: calcium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000073.question: Do you need surgery for an enlarged parathyroid gland?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000073.answer_short: Wallach says no — an enlarged parathyroid from calcium deficiency is often mislabeled a 'tumor,' but supplementing usable calcium resolves it, so don't get surgery.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000183.subject: vitamin-b1
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000183.question: What causes Korsakoff's syndrome?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000183.answer_short: Korsakoff's syndrome — recent memory loss that mimics Alzheimer's — results from chronic alcoholism and vitamin B1 deficiency tied to excess simple carbohydrate and sugar.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000184.subject: vitamin-b1
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000184.question: Can eating raw fish cause a vitamin B1 deficiency?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000184.answer_short: Yes — the flesh of some fish like smelt contains thiaminase, an enzyme that destroys thiamine; Wallach saw it cause fatal B1 deficiency in aquarium dolphins fed only raw smelt.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000185.subject: vitamin-b2
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000185.question: What causes cracks at the corners of the mouth?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000185.answer_short: Cracks at the corners of the mouth (cheilosis) are a classic sign of vitamin B2 (riboflavin) deficiency.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000186.subject: vitamin-b2
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000186.question: How much vitamin B2 should I take for cheilosis?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000186.answer_short: Wallach treats cheilosis with vitamin B2 at 75 mg three times a day, plus checking for food allergies.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000187.subject: vitamin-b3
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000187.question: How much niacin does Wallach recommend for high cholesterol?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000187.answer_short: Wallach's protocol for elevated cholesterol includes niacin at 450 mg twice a day in time-release tablets, plus EFAs, chromium, vanadium, and selenium.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000188.subject: vitamin-b3
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000188.question: Can niacin help schizophrenia?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000188.answer_short: Wallach says there is considerable evidence schizophrenia results from a severe niacin deficiency, requiring megadoses around 4,000 mg/day.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000189.subject: vitamin-b6
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000189.question: Can vitamin B6 cure epilepsy?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000189.answer_short: Wallach says vitamin B6 alone will frequently 'cure' epilepsy at 50-100 mg three times a day.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000190.subject: vitamin-b6
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000190.question: Does vitamin B6 help with alcoholism or hypoglycemia?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000190.answer_short: Wallach's alcoholism protocol includes vitamin B6 at 100 mg twice a day to help solve the underlying hypoglycemia.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000191.subject: vitamin-b9
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000191.question: Does folic acid deficiency cause spina bifida?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000191.answer_short: Yes — Wallach ties spina bifida and anencephaly to a folic acid, B12, or zinc and vitamin A deficiency in early pregnancy, and blames a Texas anencephaly cluster on folic acid and zinc shortage rather than pollution.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000192.subject: vitamin-b9
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000192.question: How does Wallach treat anemia with folic acid?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000192.answer_short: For anemia Wallach's protocol includes folic acid 15 mg for 20 days, alongside B12, iron, copper, zinc, other B vitamins, vitamins C and E, selenium, and essential fatty acids, with betaine HCl to ensure absorption.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000193.subject: vitamin-b12
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000193.question: Why does it take years for vegans to become B12 deficient?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000193.answer_short: The body recycles B12 through an intestine-to-liver loop and stores it, so a B12 deficiency in vegans may not appear for five to ten years after giving up meat.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000194.subject: vitamin-b12
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000194.question: Can a B12 deficiency cause birth defects?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000194.answer_short: Yes — Wallach's professor created spina bifida in animals in 1956 by feeding pregnant mothers diets deficient in zinc, vitamin B12, and folic acid.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000195.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000195.question: What causes hemorrhoids according to Wallach?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000195.answer_short: Wallach says hemorrhoids are primarily a copper deficiency that breaks down the elastic fibers in veins, worsened by low fiber, constipation, and lack of exercise.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000196.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000196.question: Can copper supplements bring back my natural hair color?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000196.answer_short: Wallach says supplementing with plant-derived colloidal copper can restore a person's original hair color and clear spider veins, varicose veins, and hemorrhoids.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000197.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000197.question: Can copper prevent or reverse an aneurysm, and how much should you take?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000197.answer_short: Wallach says aneurysms are most often a copper deficiency and that 2-4 mg of copper a day, if well absorbed, can prevent them; he reports one aortic aneurysm corrected by copper and confirmed on x-ray.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000198.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000198.question: Do copper bracelets work for arthritis?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000198.answer_short: Wallach recommends 2-5 mg of copper a day for joint pain and says a copper bracelet can be of great value, treating it as a real route of copper absorption.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000199.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000199.question: Is Menkes kinky hair syndrome genetic?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000199.answer_short: Wallach argues Menkes kinky hair syndrome is not truly genetic but a copper-malabsorption problem of early infancy, treatable with copper once absorption is fixed.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000200.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000200.question: How does chromium work in the body?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000200.answer_short: Chromium activates key enzymes and is the core of GTF, the glucose tolerance factor, a complex of chromium III, dinicotinic acid, and glutathione.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000201.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000201.question: Does eating sugar deplete your chromium?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000201.answer_short: Yes — Wallach says dietary sugar loads raise the rate of urinary chromium loss by 300 percent for 12 hours.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000202.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000202.question: Does chromium picolinate help with weight loss?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000202.answer_short: Wallach recommends a weight-loss support product containing chromium picolinate, which he says allows carbohydrate and fats to be burned, taken before each meal.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000203.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000203.question: What does Wallach recommend for an irregular heartbeat?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000203.answer_short: Among his cardiac-arrhythmia nutrients, he lists potassium at 500 mg three times a day, alongside magnesium, selenium, chromium and B-complex.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000204.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000204.question: Do you lose potassium when you vomit?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000204.answer_short: Yes — significant amounts of potassium are lost through vomiting, so Wallach advises replacing it with an electrolyte drink.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000205.subject: iodine
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000205.question: What causes goiter?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000205.answer_short: Goiter is a simple deficiency of iodine (and copper, molybdenum, and tyrosine) that makes the thyroid gland swell.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000206.subject: iodine
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000206.question: Is seaweed good for the thyroid?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000206.answer_short: Yes, in the studies Wallach cites, Japanese subjects developed goiter on every test food except seaweed, which was protective.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000207.subject: iodine
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000207.question: How do you treat goiter naturally?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000207.answer_short: Wallach's goiter protocol removes goitrogens, supplements iodine at 250 mcg a day plus thyroid USP, and uses kelp as a natural iodine source.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000208.subject: iodine
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000208.question: What foods block iodine or cause goiter?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000208.answer_short: Goitrogens, such as nitrates in processed meats and well water plus cabbage, broccoli, and Brussels sprouts, trigger goiter.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000209.subject: iodine
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000209.question: Can you take too much iodine? Is iodine safe?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000209.answer_short: Wallach says metallic iodine is not toxic up to 2,000 mcg a day, far above the 170 to 250 mcg most Americans get.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000210.subject: iodine
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000210.question: How did Wallach discover that nitrates cause goiter?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000210.answer_short: A farmer's flock of lambs died of goiter despite iodine in their salt block; Wallach traced it to nitrates in drought-stressed corn, his first published paper.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000211.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000211.question: Can vitamin E deficiency cause easy bruising?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000211.answer_short: Yes — Wallach says fragile capillaries that bruise easily can result from vitamin E deficiency (along with copper, vitamin K or C deficiency or blood thinners).

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000212.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000212.question: Is vitamin E good for your sex life?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000212.answer_short: Wallach recounts that in the 1960s vitamin E was popularly touted for people's sex life and longevity, part of that era's focus on vitamins.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000237.subject: vitamin-b1
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000237.question: What is Vitamin B1?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000237.answer_short: Vitamin B1 (thiamine) is a water-soluble B-complex vitamin and an essential cofactor for energy production and the metabolism of carbohydrates.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000238.subject: vitamin-b1
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000238.question: What does vitamin B1 do in the body?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000238.answer_short: Thiamine is a cofactor for energy production; it forms the coenzyme TPP that drives the oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate at the entry to the Krebs cycle.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000239.subject: vitamin-b1
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000239.question: Can vitamin B1 reverse memory loss or dementia?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000239.answer_short: Wallach cured a patient misdiagnosed with Alzheimer's — who actually had Korsakoff's syndrome, a single thiamine-deficiency disease — in one week using mega-doses of thiamine.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000240.subject: vitamin-b1
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000240.question: How was beriberi proven to be a dietary disease?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000240.answer_short: Japanese naval surgeon Takaki proved beriberi came from diet: one ship returned in 1883 with 25 dead and 144 stricken sailors, and correcting the diet on later voyages nearly eliminated it.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000241.subject: vitamin-b1
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000241.question: Why are vitamins called vitamins?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000241.answer_short: The word 'vitamin' traces to thiamine: Funk's crystalline anti-beriberi substance was a basic (vital) amine, which he named a 'vital amine' — later shortened to vitamin.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000242.subject: vitamin-b2
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000242.question: What is Vitamin B2?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000242.answer_short: Vitamin B2 (riboflavin) is a water-soluble B vitamin that acts as a cofactor for the flavin coenzymes FMN and FAD, which the body needs for energy production.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000243.subject: vitamin-b2
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000243.question: What does vitamin B2 (riboflavin) do in the body?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000243.answer_short: Riboflavin is a cofactor for the flavin coenzymes FMN and FAD that drive oxidation-reduction reactions and energy production.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000244.subject: vitamin-b3
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000244.question: What is niacin (vitamin B3)?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000244.answer_short: Niacin, or vitamin B3, is a water-soluble B vitamin the body turns into the coenzymes NAD and NADP to release energy from food; a severe deficiency causes pellagra.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000245.subject: vitamin-b3
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000245.question: What does vitamin B3 (niacin) actually do in the body?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000245.answer_short: Niacin forms the coenzymes NAD and NADP, which cells use to release energy from carbohydrates, fats, and proteins.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000246.subject: vitamin-b3
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000246.question: Why does eating a lot of corn cause pellagra?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000246.answer_short: Corn is not poisonous, but the little niacin it contains is not easily used by humans, so a corn-heavy diet leaves people niacin-deficient.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000247.subject: vitamin-b3
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000247.question: How much tryptophan does the body need to make niacin?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000247.answer_short: By convention, 60 mg of the amino acid tryptophan equals 1 mg of niacin, though studies found the amount ranged from 39 to 86 mg.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000248.subject: vitamin-b3
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000248.question: What are the side effects of too much niacin?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000248.answer_short: Overdosing on nicotinic acid can cause hot skin flushes, ulcers, liver disease, elevated blood sugar and uric acid, cardiac arrhythmia, and dry, itchy skin.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000249.subject: vitamin-b3
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000249.question: Who discovered that niacin cures pellagra?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000249.answer_short: Dr. Joseph Goldberger proved pellagra was a dietary deficiency, and in 1937 Conrad Elvehjem showed niacin (nicotinic acid) cured it.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000250.subject: vitamin-b3
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000250.question: Where did pellagra come from and why did it appear in Europe?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000250.answer_short: Pellagra was unknown in Europe until Columbus brought corn from the New World; peasants who became dependent on corn developed the disease.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000251.subject: vitamin-b5
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000251.question: Does vitamin B5 help make energy and hormones?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000251.answer_short: Yes — through coenzyme A, vitamin B5 helps release energy from carbohydrates and helps build fatty acids, steroid hormones, and acetylcholine.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000252.subject: vitamin-b5
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000252.question: Can you take too much vitamin B5?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000252.answer_short: Only at extreme amounts — pantothenic acid at 10 to 20 grams a day can cause a relative thiamine deficiency, diarrhea, and edema.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000253.subject: vitamin-b5
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000253.question: How was vitamin B5 discovered?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000253.answer_short: Scientists found pantothenic acid (vitamin B5) in the 1930s by accident, while searching for a nutrient that would make yeast grow.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000254.subject: vitamin-b5
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000254.question: What happens to animals deficient in pantothenic acid?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000254.answer_short: Animals on pantothenic-acid-deficient diets showed stunted growth, anemia, nerve damage, weak immunity, gastric ulcers, and many birth defects.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000255.subject: vitamin-b6
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000255.question: What is Vitamin B6?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000255.answer_short: Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) is a B-complex vitamin that occurs in three related forms — pyridoxine, pyridoxal, and pyridoxamine — which the body converts into active coenzymes for amino-acid, fat, and energy metabolism.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000256.subject: vitamin-b6
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000256.question: What does vitamin B6 do in the body?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000256.answer_short: Its active form PLP is a coenzyme for amino-acid, lipid and nucleic-acid metabolism and for glycogen phosphorylase.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000257.subject: vitamin-b6
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000257.question: Does vitamin B6 need other B vitamins to work?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000257.answer_short: Yes — riboflavin (B2) powers the enzyme that converts B6 into its active coenzyme form.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000258.subject: vitamin-b6
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000258.question: Can you take too much vitamin B6?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000258.answer_short: Yes — excess B6 can cause peripheral neuropathy, with nerve damage in the fingers and legs.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000259.subject: vitamin-b6
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000259.question: Are most people deficient in vitamin B6?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000259.answer_short: A 1980 US survey found half of those surveyed consumed less than 70% of the RDA for pyridoxine.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000260.subject: vitamin-b9
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000260.question: What is folate?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000260.answer_short: Folate — vitamin B-9, also called folic acid or folacin — is an essential B vitamin the body needs to build DNA, RNA, and red blood cells. Wallach calls its deficiency perhaps the most common vitamin deficiency in humans.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000261.subject: vitamin-b9
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000261.question: What does folic acid do in the body?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000261.answer_short: Folic acid works as a coenzyme that shuttles single carbon units in amino acid and DNA/RNA synthesis, working hand-in-hand with vitamin B12.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000262.subject: vitamin-b9
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000262.question: Can you be deficient in folic acid even if you take enough of it?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000262.answer_short: Yes — because vitamin B12 is needed to release folate into a usable form, a B12 deficiency causes a folic acid deficiency even when folic acid intake is optimal.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000263.subject: vitamin-b9
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000263.question: What medications interfere with folic acid?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000263.answer_short: Wallach says many drugs block folic acid absorption and metabolism, including methotrexate, aspirin, oral contraceptives, anti-convulsants, anti-psoriatic drugs, and cancer chemotherapy.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000264.subject: vitamin-b9
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000264.question: Can you take too much folic acid?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000264.answer_short: Yes — Wallach warns that an overdose of folic acid can cause a relative zinc deficiency by impairing zinc absorption.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000265.subject: vitamin-b9
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000265.question: Who discovered folic acid?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000265.answer_short: In 1930 Lucy Wills and her team reported that yeast contained a substance that could cure macrocytic anemia in pregnant women; folic acid itself was not isolated until 1946.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000266.subject: vitamin-b12
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000266.question: How are vitamin B12 and folic acid related?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000266.answer_short: B12 is required to release folate from its bound form, so a B12 deficiency creates a folic acid deficiency even when folate intake is high.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000267.subject: vitamin-b12
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000267.question: Where does vitamin B12 come from?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000267.answer_short: B12 comes from animal products and bacterial fermentation, because only bacteria, fungi, and algae can actually make it — plants and animals cannot.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000268.subject: vitamin-b12
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000268.question: What is the difference between cyanocobalamin and the natural forms of B12?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000268.answer_short: Cyanocobalamin is the primary commercial form of B12 in supplements; the body strips off the cyanide and converts it to the metabolically useful forms found in the tissues.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000269.subject: vitamin-b12
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000269.question: What causes vitamin B12 deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000269.answer_short: B12 deficiency comes from a poor diet, low stomach acid, salt deficiency, and gluten intolerance.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000270.subject: vitamin-b12
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000270.question: Can you take too much vitamin B12?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000270.answer_short: Wallach reports that no clear toxicity has been reported from daily oral B12 in doses of up to 100 mcg.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000271.subject: vitamin-b12
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000271.question: How was vitamin B12 discovered?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000271.answer_short: The search began in 1926 after doctors found that eating a pound of raw liver a day cured pernicious anemia; the pure vitamin was finally isolated in 1948.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000272.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000272.question: How does copper help the body use oxygen?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000272.answer_short: Copper proteins carry and process oxygen and drive cellular respiration; in mollusks the copper-based carrier hemocyanin even makes their blood blue.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000273.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000273.question: What causes Kawasaki disease?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000273.answer_short: Wallach says Kawasaki disease is not genetic but a congenital copper deficiency that leaves a baby with a weak coronary artery aneurysm, later infected by strep.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000274.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000274.question: Is mad cow disease caused by copper deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000274.answer_short: Wallach argues that mad cow disease (BSE) and CJD are copper-deficiency diseases, not prion infections, pointing to identical brain lesions and copper-poor soils where cases cluster.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000275.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000275.question: How do you test chromium levels, and how much is in the body?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000275.answer_short: Wallach says hair analysis is far more accurate than blood for chromium because hair holds ten times more, and the body contains about 1.5 mg under optimal conditions.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000276.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000276.question: How much chromium do you actually absorb from food?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000276.answer_short: Very little — 50 to 100 mcg of inorganic chromium from food yields only 0.25 to 0.5 mcg usable, whereas 25 percent of chelated chromium is absorbed.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000277.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000277.question: Is type 2 diabetes genetic or caused by a mineral deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000277.answer_short: Wallach insists type 2 diabetes is not genetically transmitted — it is in fact a simple mineral deficiency.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000278.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000278.question: What was chromium used for in ancient times?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000278.answer_short: Wallach recounts that over 2,000 years ago the Chinese coated the Terracotta Army's bronze weapons with chromium oxide, which kept them from corroding.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000279.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000279.question: What is Vitamin E?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000279.answer_short: Vitamin E is a fat-soluble antioxidant vitamin — actually a family of compounds called tocopherols — that protects cell membranes and red blood cells from oxidative damage.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000280.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000280.question: What does vitamin E do for the body?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000280.answer_short: Vitamin E slows aging and preserves telomere length; combined with selenium it reduces the risk of certain cancers, and Wallach also links it to a lower risk of Alzheimer's disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, muscular dystrophy and cystic fibrosis.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000281.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000281.question: Can you take too much vitamin E?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000281.answer_short: Wallach calls vitamin E extremely safe by mouth — most adults have no problem up to 800 mg a day with no signs of toxicity.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000282.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000282.question: Why does Wallach say Alzheimer's disease isn't genetic?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000282.answer_short: Because supplementing with only vitamin E measurably improved advanced Alzheimer's patients — and a vitamin can't change a truly genetic disease.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000283.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000283.question: How was vitamin E discovered?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000283.answer_short: Vitamin E was recognized in 1922 when female rats were found to need an unknown dietary factor to carry pregnancies to term without miscarrying.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000284.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000284.question: Can vitamin E cure muscular dystrophy?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000284.answer_short: In livestock, Wallach says injecting selenium and vitamin E into animals with 'white muscle disease' (muscular dystrophy) cures it within days.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000031.subject: vitamin-b3
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000031.question: Who first described pellagra?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000031.answer_short: Gaspar Casal published the first account of pellagra — a vitamin B3 deficiency — in Spain in 1755, calling it a 'new disease.'

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000032.subject: vitamin-b6
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000032.question: What foods are high in vitamin B6?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000032.answer_short: Wallach notes that a handful of pistachios provides twenty-five percent of the USDA recommended daily value for vitamin B6.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000033.subject: vitamin-b9
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000033.question: Does folic acid help prevent breast cancer?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000033.answer_short: Wallach cites research that folic acid supplementation can reduce the risk of breast cancer for nondrinkers and drinkers alike.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000034.subject: vitamin-b9
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000034.question: What foods are high in folic acid?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000034.answer_short: Wallach points to liver as rich in folic acid (along with iron, copper, selenium, B12, and vitamins A, C, and D), citing Whipple's 1925 experiment where liver-fed dogs rebuilt red blood cells fastest.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000035.subject: vitamin-b9
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000035.question: Why did it take so long to add folic acid to food?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000035.answer_short: Wallach says the FDA's 1963 restrictions on folic acid stayed in place for thirty-one years; the FDA only ordered folic acid fortification of flour in 1996, and by 1998 the spina bifida rate had dropped twenty percent.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000036.subject: vitamin-b12
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000036.question: Can a low-salt diet cause a B12 deficiency?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000036.answer_short: Yes — salt is the raw material for stomach acid, and stomach acid is needed to activate the intrinsic factor that absorbs vitamin B12.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000037.subject: vitamin-b12
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000037.question: What is pernicious anemia and how is it related to B12?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000037.answer_short: Pernicious anemia is a fatal anemia, first reported in 1849, caused by missing vitamin B12; absorbing B12 requires both stomach acid and an acid-dependent 'intrinsic factor.'

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000038.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000038.question: What foods are high in copper?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000038.answer_short: Wallach points to animal organs—heart, liver, kidneys, and brains—as rich stores of copper along with zinc and selenium.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000039.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000039.question: Are cashews a good source of copper?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000039.answer_short: Yes, Wallach notes a handful of cashews supplies about 30 percent of the recommended daily allowance of copper, along with magnesium and iron.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000040.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000040.question: Did Einstein really die of a copper deficiency?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000040.answer_short: Wallach says Einstein died of a simple copper deficiency, the same ruptured-aneurysm problem he had already eliminated in turkeys years earlier just by raising copper in their feed.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000041.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000041.question: What is chromium?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000041.answer_short: Chromium is an essential trace mineral the body must have for normal glucose metabolism, working hand-in-hand with insulin to control blood sugar.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000042.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000042.question: What is chromium and what does it do?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000042.answer_short: Chromium is an essential trace mineral required for normal glucose metabolism, and its job is tied directly to how insulin works.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000043.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000043.question: Which form of chromium is active in the body?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000043.answer_short: Only trivalent chromium is biologically active, and it does more than manage blood sugar — it also drives amino acid transport and protein synthesis.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000044.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000044.question: What are the symptoms of chromium deficiency?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000044.answer_short: Chromium deficiency shows up as glucose intolerance, poor growth, peripheral neuropathy, muscle and protein loss, and a lowered respiratory quotient.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000045.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000045.question: What causes intense sugar, carb, and chocolate cravings?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000045.answer_short: According to Wallach, obsessive carb cravings and the 'munchies' — especially for chocolate and sweets — are sure signs of a chromium and vanadium deficiency.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000046.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000046.question: Can chromium replace insulin injections?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000046.answer_short: In 1977 K. N. Jeejeebhoy reported that intravenous chromium eliminated the need for medical insulin in human diabetics and reversed their peripheral neuropathy.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000047.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000047.question: What happens to animals that lack potassium?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000047.answer_short: Potassium-deficient rats turn hyper-alert and hyperactive and lick everything in sight — cage, equipment, each other, even urine.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000048.subject: potassium
