WAL-CLM-HELLS-000048.question: Can you actually become deficient in potassium?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000048.answer_short: Naturally it's rare because grains, fruits and vegetables are potassium-rich, but diuretics or a junk-food diet can cause it.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000049.subject: iodine
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000049.question: Why is table salt iodized?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000049.answer_short: Iodized salt was introduced in 1925 (Morton Salt) specifically to prevent goiter by restoring iodine to the diet.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000050.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000050.question: What foods are high in vitamin E?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000050.answer_short: When vitamin E was first identified as a fertility factor, it was found abundant in green leafy vegetables and wheat germ.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000051.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000051.question: Which foods are high in vitamin E?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000051.answer_short: Nuts are a rich source; Wallach notes hazelnuts, almonds and walnuts all supply vitamin E, with 24 hazelnuts giving about 20% of the daily value.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000052.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000052.question: Does vitamin E help with Alzheimer's disease?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000052.answer_short: Wallach cites studies showing vitamin E can ease memory loss and slow decline in Alzheimer's patients, delaying the need for nursing-home care.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000053.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000053.question: Does vitamin E help prevent cancer?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000053.answer_short: In a five-year China study Wallach cites, beta carotene, vitamin E and selenium together gave 13% fewer cancer deaths and 21% fewer stomach-cancer deaths.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000054.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000054.question: Why is it called vitamin E?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000054.answer_short: The newly found fertility factor was fat-soluble but not related to any known vitamin, so it was named vitamin E.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000294.subject: vitamin-b1
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000294.question: What are the symptoms of vitamin B1 deficiency?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000294.answer_short: Mild thiamine deficiency causes mental confusion, muscle weakness, fatigue and appetite loss; chronic deficiency progresses to polyneuritis and congestive heart failure.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000295.subject: vitamin-b1
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000295.question: Does eating sugar and carbs use up vitamin B1?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000295.answer_short: Yes — metabolizing carbohydrates requires thiamine, while fats can be burned for energy without it, so fats 'spare' thiamine and a high-carb diet raises the need for it.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000296.subject: vitamin-b2
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000296.question: What foods are high in vitamin B2 (riboflavin)?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000296.answer_short: Riboflavin is found in milk, cheddar and cottage cheese, organ meats, eggs, and green leafy vegetables.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000297.subject: vitamin-b2
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000297.question: How was vitamin B2 (riboflavin) discovered?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000297.answer_short: Riboflavin was first seen in 1879 as a yellow-green pigment in milk whey, isolated in 1932, then synthesized and named in 1935 by Kuhn.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000298.subject: vitamin-b3
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000298.question: What are the symptoms of vitamin B3 (niacin) deficiency?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000298.answer_short: Early niacin deficiency brings muscle weakness, poor appetite, indigestion, and skin eruptions; severe deficiency becomes pellagra.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000299.subject: vitamin-b5
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000299.question: What is Vitamin B5?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000299.answer_short: Vitamin B5, or pantothenic acid, is a water-soluble B-complex vitamin and the core building block of coenzyme A - the molecule the body uses to turn carbohydrates, fats, and proteins into energy.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000300.subject: vitamin-b6
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000300.question: Does vitamin B6 help children with seizures or convulsions?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000300.answer_short: Some children have convulsions from an inborn error of B6 metabolism and need large daily B6 doses to make GABA and prevent permanent retardation.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000301.subject: vitamin-b6
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000301.question: When was vitamin B6 discovered?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000301.answer_short: Pyridoxine (vitamin B6) was identified in 1938 as a distinct part of the B-complex, and is really a family of three related compounds.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000302.subject: vitamin-b9
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000302.question: Why can taking folic acid be risky if you have a B12 deficiency?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000302.answer_short: Folic acid can mask a B12 deficiency — it corrects the anemia while the nerve damage silently keeps getting worse.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000303.subject: vitamin-b9
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000303.question: How common is folic acid deficiency?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000303.answer_short: Wallach says folic acid deficiency may be the most common vitamin deficiency in humans.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000304.subject: vitamin-b12
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000304.question: What is Vitamin B12?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000304.answer_short: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is a red, water-soluble vitamin whose color and biological activity both come from a single cobalt atom at the center of its molecule.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000305.subject: vitamin-b12
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000305.question: What is vitamin B12?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000305.answer_short: Vitamin B12 is a red, water-soluble vitamin whose color and function come from a single cobalt atom at its center.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000306.subject: vitamin-b12
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000306.question: Why do older people need vitamin B12 shots?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000306.answer_short: B12 needs an intrinsic factor plus stomach acid (pH 2.0 or less) to be absorbed, so people with low stomach acid — often from salt-restricted diets — cannot absorb it and are given B12 shots instead.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000307.subject: vitamin-b12
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000307.question: Can folic acid hide a vitamin B12 deficiency?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000307.answer_short: Yes — in pernicious anemia, folic acid improves the anemia but lets the nerve and gut damage keep progressing, an effect Wallach calls the 'masking effect.'

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000308.subject: vitamin-b12
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000308.question: Why is vitamin B12 called cyanocobalamin?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000308.answer_short: The first B12 molecule isolated in the lab contained a cyanide group, which gave it the name cyanocobalamin.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000309.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000309.question: What is copper?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000309.answer_short: Copper is an essential nutrient for every living organism and a cofactor for many hundreds of enzymes; Wallach considers copper deficiency widespread, common, and behind many everyday diseases.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000310.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000310.question: Is copper oxide a good source of copper?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000310.answer_short: No, Wallach classes copper oxide as a metallic mineral that is only 8 to 12 percent absorbable, dropping to 3 to 5 percent after age 35 to 40.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000311.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000311.question: What gives rubies and emeralds their color?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000311.answer_short: The radiant colors of many gems come from trace chromium — it makes rubies red and emeralds green.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000312.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000312.question: Where is chromium found in nature?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000312.answer_short: Chromium occurs from about 100 ppm in igneous rocks down to trace levels in water, and in the body it accumulates in RNA and insulin.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000313.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000313.question: Are Americans getting less chromium than they used to?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000313.answer_short: Average American serum chromium has fallen steadily since 1948, from 28-1000 down to about 0.13 by 1985.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000314.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000314.question: How does the body regulate potassium levels?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000314.answer_short: Adrenal-cortex hormones and the pituitary control sodium, potassium and chloride balance; adrenal failure (Addison's disease) causes potassium loss.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000315.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000315.question: Who discovered potassium?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000315.answer_short: Sir Humphrey Davy first isolated elemental potassium in 1807 using electrolysis.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000316.subject: iodine
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000316.question: What is iodine?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000316.answer_short: Iodine is a violet-black halogen element the body needs to build thyroid hormone; run short of it and the thyroid swells into a goiter.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000317.subject: iodine
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000317.question: Does the body absorb iodine well?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000317.answer_short: Yes, Wallach says the metallic form of iodine is absorbed at almost a 1:1 ratio, far better than iron (1:10) or chromium (1:100).

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000318.subject: iodine
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000318.question: Where does the name iodine come from?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000318.answer_short: Iodine's name comes from the Greek word iodes, meaning "violet-colored," after the violet gas it forms.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000319.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000319.question: Can a lack of vitamin E cause infertility or miscarriage?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000319.answer_short: Yes; Wallach lists miscarriage, fetal reabsorption, testicular atrophy and birth defects among the effects of vitamin E deficiency.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000320.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000320.question: How does vitamin E slow aging?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000320.answer_short: Vitamin E protects the fatty membranes of your cells from peroxidation (free-radical damage), and that protection is tied to its anti-aging effect.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000321.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000321.question: Do vitamin E and selenium work together?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000321.answer_short: Yes; vitamin E and selenium partner in the cell membrane, with selenium activating glutathione peroxidase to destroy peroxides before they cause damage.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000322.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000322.question: Who discovered vitamin E?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000322.answer_short: Vitamin E was first identified by Evans and Bishop in 1922, when they found that infertility in rats fed vegetable-oil extracts could be reversed.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000323.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000323.question: Why is vitamin E called tocopherol?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000323.answer_short: Tocopherol comes from the Greek 'tokos,' meaning 'offspring,' reflecting vitamin E's link to fertility and reproduction.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000506.subject: vitamin-b3
WAL-CLM-LETS-000506.question: Is high-dose niacin used to treat mental illness?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000506.answer_short: In orthomolecular medicine, niacinamide is given at 3,000 mg per day for psychosis — far above the tiny 1.5 mg RDA for niacin.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000507.subject: vitamin-b9
WAL-CLM-LETS-000507.question: Did Wallach's own family have health problems doctors missed?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000507.answer_short: Yes — Wallach says pediatricians missed a folic acid deficiency anemia (and a fractured arm) in his children, and misdiagnosed his son's food allergies as learning disabilities.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000508.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-LETS-000508.question: What causes hypoglycemia?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000508.answer_short: Hypoglycemia is almost always caused by malabsorption of chromium and vanadium plus sugar and refined flour dumping chromium in the urine by up to 300%.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000509.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-LETS-000509.question: How much chromium should I take for low blood sugar?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000509.answer_short: Chromium and vanadium are Wallach's "magic bullets" for hypoglycemia at 50-200 mcg three times daily, but insulin users should start at 25 mcg.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000510.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-LETS-000510.question: What is a normal potassium level in a blood test?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000510.answer_short: Wallach gives a normal blood potassium range of 3.5 to 4.4 mEq/L.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000511.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-LETS-000511.question: Can vitamin E help muscular dystrophy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000511.answer_short: Wallach says muscular dystrophy will be arrested or cured if selenium and vitamin E are given by injection at the very first onset of symptoms.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000343.subject: vitamin-b9
WAL-CLM-RARE-000343.question: Does folic acid alone prevent spina bifida?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000343.answer_short: No — Wallach says folic acid supplementation only prevents 50% of spina bifida; zinc supplementation prevents the other 50%.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000344.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-RARE-000344.question: Why does copper deficiency turn hair gray?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000344.answer_short: Copper is the cofactor for tyrosinase, the enzyme that makes hair pigment, so without it hair turns white, silver or gray.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000345.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-RARE-000345.question: Can copper deficiency during pregnancy cause birth defects?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000345.answer_short: Wallach says copper deficiency in a pregnant mother causes congenital heart defects like Kawasaki disease and brain defects like cerebral palsy.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000346.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-RARE-000346.question: Does molybdenum interact with copper?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000346.answer_short: Wallach cites Dick's finding of a three-way interaction between copper, molybdenum and inorganic sulfate.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000347.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-RARE-000347.question: What are the earliest signs of copper deficiency in infants?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000347.answer_short: Neutropenia and leukopenia are the earliest indicators; cow's-milk-fed infants often develop anemia.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000348.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-RARE-000348.question: How much copper does the body need each day?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000348.answer_short: A well-nourished adult body holds 80-120 mg of copper; the daily need is 0.08 mg/kg for newborns, 0.04 for toddlers and 0.03 for adults.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000349.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000349.question: What is chromium picolinate?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000349.answer_short: Chromium picolinate is a chelated form of chromium; chelated minerals are about 40% bioavailable, far better than metallic minerals.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000350.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000350.question: What is potassium?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000350.answer_short: Potassium is an essential mineral — the major positively charged ion inside your cells — that runs fluid balance, nerve signaling and muscle activity, and makes up about five percent of the body's total mineral content.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000351.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000351.question: What does high potassium on a hair analysis mean?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000351.answer_short: Wallach says elevated hair levels of sodium, potassium and chloride actually indicate an essential fatty acid deficiency, because the skin glands lose electrolytes instead of conserving them.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000352.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000352.question: Does potassium affect blood pressure and salt sensitivity?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000352.answer_short: Wallach reports that in Black and elderly white people with high blood pressure, low intake of calcium and potassium — not high salt — is what drives salt sensitivity.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000353.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000353.question: Is potassium one of the essential minerals the body needs?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000353.answer_short: Yes — Wallach lists potassium among 'The 60 Essential Elements, Metals and Minerals' the human body requires.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000354.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000354.question: Is potassium radioactive?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000354.answer_short: One rare form, potassium 40, is radioactive — it decays into argon 40 with a half-life of 1.3 billion years, which is why geologists use the 'potassium-argon' method to date rocks.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000355.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-RARE-000355.question: What diseases are linked to a vitamin E deficiency?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000355.answer_short: Wallach ties vitamin E deficiency to several leading killers — cardiomyopathy, coronary and cerebrovascular disease, cancer, and Alzheimer's disease.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000356.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-RARE-000356.question: Can a vitamin E deficiency cause intestinal disease?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000356.answer_short: Yes — Wallach lists vitamin E among the nutrient deficiencies that result in intestinal disease.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000357.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-RARE-000357.question: Why does Wallach think vitamin E can help Alzheimer's?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000357.answer_short: Because in poultry a brain-wasting disease called 'star-gazing' (encephalomalacia) is prevented, and if caught early cured, with high doses of vitamin E and selenium.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000043.subject: vitamin-b1
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000043.question: What is beriberi and what causes it?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000043.answer_short: Beriberi is the classic thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency disease; Wallach saw it commonly in Africa, where it caused congestive heart failure.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000064.subject: vitamin-b2
WAL-CLM-LETS-000064.question: How much vitamin B2 should I take a day?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000064.answer_short: Wallach's supplement table lists riboflavin (vitamin B-2) at 50 mg a day - far above the 1.6 mg RDA - with a higher range of 200 to 500 mg.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000029.subject: vitamin-b2
WAL-CLM-LETS-000029.question: What are the signs of vitamin B2 (riboflavin) deficiency?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000029.answer_short: Riboflavin deficiency can cause cheilosis, cataracts, blurred vision, hair loss, dermatitis, depression, and growth retardation.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000059.subject: vitamin-b3
WAL-CLM-LETS-000059.question: How much niacin should I take each day?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000059.answer_short: Wallach's baseline program lists niacin at a 50 mg daily supplement (vs an 18 mg RDA), with a pharmacologic range of 2,000 to 6,000 mg in time-release form.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000049.subject: vitamin-b3
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000049.question: Is niacin important for blood sugar or diabetes?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000049.answer_short: Yes — niacin is part of the GTF (glucose tolerance factor), so Wallach's diabetes protocol makes a point of including it.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000021.subject: vitamin-b5
WAL-CLM-LETS-000021.question: What are the symptoms of vitamin B5 deficiency?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000021.answer_short: B5 deficiency can cause burning feet, eczema, hair loss, fatigue, insomnia, depression, low blood pressure, and a fast heartbeat.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000115.subject: vitamin-b5
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000115.question: How much vitamin B5 should I take daily?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000115.answer_short: Wallach recommends 25 to 100 mg of vitamin B5 (pantothenic acid) per day for adults and children over 9.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000060.subject: vitamin-b5
WAL-CLM-LETS-000060.question: What is the therapeutic dose of vitamin B5, and how does it compare to the RDA?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000060.answer_short: The RDA for pantothenic acid is only 4 mg, but Wallach's baseline program calls for 50 mg, with therapeutic doses of 300 to 1,000 mg per day.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000027.subject: vitamin-b6
WAL-CLM-LETS-000027.question: What are the symptoms of vitamin B6 deficiency?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000027.answer_short: Wallach links B6 (pyridoxine) deficiency to acne, hair loss, anemia, depression, fatigue, seizures, and many skin and nerve problems.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000008.subject: vitamin-b6
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000008.question: Does vitamin B6 help with morning sickness?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000008.answer_short: Wallach says the morning sickness of early pregnancy is thought to be due to pyridoxine (B6) deficiency.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000063.subject: vitamin-b6
WAL-CLM-LETS-000063.question: How much vitamin B6 should I take?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000063.answer_short: Wallach's baseline program lists 50 mg of B6 a day (vs the 2.2 mg RDA), rising to 200-500 mg as a therapeutic dose.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000010.subject: vitamin-b9
WAL-CLM-LETS-000010.question: What are the symptoms of folic acid deficiency?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000010.answer_short: Folic acid deficiency shows up as megaloblastic anemia, birth defects like spina bifida, fatigue, geographic tongue, memory loss, paranoia, insomnia, and more.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000080.subject: vitamin-b12
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000080.question: What does vitamin B12 do in the body?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000080.answer_short: B12 helps build DNA and RNA, forms the myelin that insulates nerves, and is required to make red blood cells.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000116.subject: vitamin-b12
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000116.question: How much vitamin B12 should I take daily?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000116.answer_short: Wallach's recommended daily multiple lists vitamin B12 (as methylcobalamin) at 400 mcg for adults and children over 9.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000040.subject: vitamin-b12
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000040.question: What are the symptoms of vitamin B12 deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000040.answer_short: B12 deficiency causes pernicious anemia, dementia and neuropsychiatric changes, nerve demyelination and neuropathy, a sore tongue, general weakness, and liver disease.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000003.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000003.question: Does copper deficiency cause gray hair?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000003.answer_short: Yes; Wallach says copper deficiency shows up first as white, gray, or silver hair because copper is the cofactor needed to make hair pigment.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000063.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000063.question: Can copper deficiency cause violent or aggressive behavior?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000063.answer_short: Wallach lists violent behavior, blind rage, explosive behavior, and criminal behavior among the symptoms of copper deficiency.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000100.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000100.question: What does copper do in the body?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000100.answer_short: Copper is needed for RNA and DNA, lysyl oxidase and elastic fibers, melanin (skin and hair color), and the electron transport that powers cellular respiration.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000107.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000107.question: How does copper keep arteries and veins strong?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000107.answer_short: Copper runs the enzyme lysyl oxidase that turns proelastin into elastin, so a deficiency weakens vessel walls and produces spider veins, varicose veins, hemorrhoids and aneurysms.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000180.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000180.question: Does copper affect the thyroid and iodine?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000180.answer_short: Yes, Wallach says copper is a cofactor needed to use iodine efficiently, so copper-deficient soils cause goiter even where iodine is adequate.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000142.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-RARE-000142.question: What causes high copper levels in the blood?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000142.answer_short: Wallach says copper rises 100% in pregnancy and on oral contraceptives, and is elevated by infection, liver disease and pellagra.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000049.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-LETS-000049.question: How much copper should I take a day?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000049.answer_short: In Wallach's baseline program the copper RDA is 2 mg, the true supplement need is 3 to 4 mg, and the pharmacologic daily dose is 4 to 6 mg.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000099.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000099.question: What are the signs of copper deficiency?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000099.answer_short: Wallach lists white, grey and silver hair, loss of skin pigment (vitiligo), and dry brittle hair among the first signs, alongside aneurysms, varicose veins, anemia and arthritis.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000104.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000104.question: How common are aneurysms from copper deficiency?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000104.answer_short: Wallach says 4 to 6 of every 100 Americans autopsied died of a ruptured aneurysm, and names Einstein, Franklin D. Roosevelt, Paavo Airola, Conway Twitty and John Ritter as copper-deficiency aneurysm deaths.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000009.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-LETS-000009.question: Can you take too much copper?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000009.answer_short: Yes, Wallach's chart lists copper toxicity as depression, irritability, joint pain, muscle pain and nervousness.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000129.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-RARE-000129.question: What do copper levels in hair analysis reveal about mental illness?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000129.answer_short: Wallach reports hair analysis shows high copper in schizophrenia and low copper in violent, sociopathic behavior.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000004.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000004.question: How was it discovered that copper deficiency causes aneurysms?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000004.answer_short: Turkeys raised on copper-poor complete feed pellets died in droves from ruptured aortic aneurysms; the next year, doubling the copper in the feed stopped the deaths entirely, because copper is required to manufacture the heavy elastic fibers in arteries.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000123.subject: copper
WAL-CLM-RARE-000123.question: Is cerebral palsy linked to copper deficiency?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000123.answer_short: Wallach says the copper-deficiency disease in newborn lambs produces demyelination changes identical to human cerebral palsy.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000116.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000116.question: What diseases does chromium deficiency cause?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000116.answer_short: Wallach links chromium deficiency to low blood sugar, prediabetes, diabetes, ADD/ADHD, depression, bipolar disease, infertility, and a shortened life span, among many others.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000046.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000046.question: Can chromium prevent or cure diabetes?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000046.answer_short: Since 1958 it has been known that supplemental chromium will prevent and treat both diabetes and hypoglycemia.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000017.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000017.question: Can a chromium deficiency shorten your life?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000017.answer_short: Yes — Wallach says chromium deficiency causes a wide variety of clinical diseases and a shortened life expectancy, made worse by a concurrent vanadium deficiency.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000043.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000043.question: Do baby formulas contain chromium?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000043.answer_short: No human infant formula has more than 12 minerals — chromium, vanadium, and lithium are absent — while dog food has 40.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000016.subject: chromium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000016.question: Does chromium supplementation extend lifespan?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000016.answer_short: Gary Evans of Bemidji State University showed chromium supplementation increased laboratory animals' lifespan by 33.3 percent.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000192.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000192.question: What does potassium do in the body?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000192.answer_short: Potassium is the major positively-charged mineral inside your cells, running enzyme systems, fluid balance and nerve-muscle activity.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000193.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000193.question: How much potassium do you need per day?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000193.answer_short: Because the body stores essentially none, Wallach says it needs a significant daily intake of 5,000 mg.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000137.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000137.question: Why are potassium supplements limited to only 99 mg?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000137.answer_short: Wallach's book notes the FDA restricts the amount of potassium allowed in a supplement to 99 mg.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000062.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-LETS-000062.question: How much potassium does Wallach recommend supplementing daily?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000062.answer_short: In his Base Line Nutritional Supplement Program for adults, Wallach lists potassium at 5,500 mg per day — far above the RDA of 1,875 mg.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000374.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-LETS-000374.question: What deficiency causes muscle cramps?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000374.answer_short: Wallach calls a muscle cramp a 'mini convulsion' caused by deficiencies of calcium, magnesium, potassium, selenium and/or vitamin E.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000194.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000194.question: What are the signs of potassium deficiency?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000194.answer_short: Muscular weakness and mental apathy are the hallmark signs, and the most serious event is low-potassium (hypokalemic) heart failure.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000025.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-LETS-000025.question: What are the symptoms of too little or too much potassium?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000025.answer_short: Deficiency ranges from arrhythmia, fatigue and muscle weakness to depression and edema; toxicity can cause cardiac arrest.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000023.subject: iodine
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000023.question: What does iodine do in the body?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000023.answer_short: Iodine combines with the amino acid tyrosine to build the thyroid hormone thyroxin, and it is essential to all vertebrates.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000149.subject: iodine
WAL-CLM-RARE-000149.question: Can you have enough iodine and still get goiter?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000149.answer_short: Yes, Wallach says copper is required to use iodine, so a copper deficiency can cause goiter even where iodine is adequate.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000013.subject: iodine
WAL-CLM-LETS-000013.question: What are the signs of iodine deficiency?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000013.answer_short: Iodine deficiency shows up as goiter, fatigue, hypothyroidism, a low basal body temperature, and weight gain.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000177.subject: iodine
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000177.question: Why are goiter and hypothyroidism so common now?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000177.answer_short: Wallach blames the epidemic on Americans cutting back salt on their doctors' advice, which stripped iodine from their diets.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000033.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000033.question: What are the signs of vitamin E deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000033.answer_short: Wallach links vitamin E deficiency to Alzheimer's, hemolytic anemia, infertility, a weakened immune system, age spots, heart disease, fibrocystic breast disease, muscle problems and higher cancer risk.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000075.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-LETS-000075.question: How much vitamin E should I take?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000075.answer_short: In his Let's Play Doctor supplement table, the vitamin E row lists 15 IU, 400 IU and 1,200 IU per day across its three dose columns.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000175.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-LETS-000175.question: Can you put vitamin E oil on your skin?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000175.answer_short: Yes; Wallach recommends applying vitamin E oil directly to the skin, for example on burns and sunburn.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000275.subject: vitamin-e
WAL-CLM-LETS-000275.question: Does vitamin E help fibrocystic breast disease?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000275.answer_short: Yes; Wallach's treatment for fibrocystic breast disease includes vitamin E at 800 to 1,200 IU per day, along with avoiding caffeine.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000213.subject: vitamin-k
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000213.question: Can vitamin K help with easy bruising?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000213.answer_short: For ecchymosis (easy bruising), Wallach's treatment includes vitamin K at 15 mg/day along with vitamin C, vitamin E, alfalfa and plenty of green vegetables.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000214.subject: vitamin-k
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000214.question: Can a vitamin K deficiency cause nosebleeds?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000214.answer_short: Yes — Wallach says nosebleeds (epistaxis) are usually the result of vitamin K and/or vitamin C deficiency.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000215.subject: biotin
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000215.question: How do you treat dandruff or seborrheic dermatitis with biotin?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000215.answer_short: Wallach's protocol for seborrheic dermatitis (dandruff, cradle cap) uses biotin at 100 mcg three times daily plus folic acid, B6, vitamin E, EFAs, vitamin A, zinc, and Selsun Blue shampoo.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000216.subject: choline
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000216.question: How do choline, B12 and folic acid work together?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000216.answer_short: Choline joins vitamin B12/cobalt, folic acid and methionine to transfer single-carbon methyl groups used to build RNA and DNA.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000217.subject: choline
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000217.question: Is phosphatidylcholine better than lecithin?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000217.answer_short: Wallach says lecithin is useful but phosphatidyl choline is the more efficient form of choline.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000218.subject: choline
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000218.question: Does choline help seizures?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000218.answer_short: For absence attacks (petit mal seizures), Wallach's treatment leads with choline at 4 grams a day.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000219.subject: choline
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000219.question: Is carpal tunnel syndrome caused by choline deficiency?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000219.answer_short: Wallach says carpal tunnel syndrome is caused by a deficiency of arsenic, manganese and choline, and treats it nutritionally rather than with wrist surgery.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000220.subject: inositol
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000220.question: What dose of inositol is used for cataracts?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000220.answer_short: Wallach includes inositol at 150 mg/day in his cataract treatment protocol.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000285.subject: vitamin-k
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000285.question: What is Vitamin K?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000285.answer_short: Vitamin K is a fat-soluble vitamin your liver needs to make prothrombin and other blood-clotting proteins and to lay calcium down properly in bone — so it governs both normal clotting and bone strength.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000286.subject: vitamin-k
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000286.question: What does vitamin K do in the body?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000286.answer_short: Vitamin K is a fat-soluble vitamin the liver needs to make prothrombin and other clotting proteins and to deposit calcium properly in bone.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000287.subject: vitamin-k
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000287.question: Does your body make its own vitamin K?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000287.answer_short: Yes — Wallach says roughly half of your vitamin K requirement is produced by probiotic bacteria in the colon.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000288.subject: vitamin-k
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000288.question: What are the different forms of vitamin K and where does it come from?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000288.answer_short: Vitamin K comes in two forms — K1 (phylloquinone) from plants and K2 (menaquinones) made by gut bacteria — and is concentrated in foods like alfalfa and hog liver fat.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000289.subject: vitamin-k
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000289.question: Can you take too much vitamin K?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000289.answer_short: Wallach says overdose signs include jaundice in newborns, and that injected phylloquinone or large doses of synthetic menadione can cause serious reactions and even death.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000290.subject: vitamin-k
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000290.question: Why is it called vitamin K?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000290.answer_short: Dam named it vitamin K after 'Koagulation' (coagulation), because the nutrient resolved bleeding diseases that no other vitamin could cure.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000291.subject: biotin
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000291.question: What is biotin?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000291.answer_short: Biotin — also called vitamin H or coenzyme R — is a sulfur-containing B vitamin the body needs for glucose metabolism and the production of fatty acids.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000292.subject: biotin
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000292.question: What does biotin do in the body?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000292.answer_short: Biotin is a sulfur-containing vitamin required for glucose metabolism and the production of fatty acids, working through enzymes that carry carboxyl units and fix carbon dioxide.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000293.subject: biotin
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000293.question: Can you take too much biotin? Is biotin toxic?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000293.answer_short: No credible toxicity has been reported from large biotin doses, even above 10 mg daily, and its lethal dose is unknown.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000294.subject: biotin
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000294.question: Can large doses of biotin overcome an inborn error of metabolism?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000294.answer_short: Yes; Wallach says multiple carboxylase deficiencies from defective holocarboxylase synthetase can be overcome in an epigenetic fashion with large doses of biotin.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000295.subject: biotin
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000295.question: How was biotin discovered?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000295.answer_short: Biotin was found through the 'egg white syndrome': rats fed egg whites developed skin inflammation, baldness, paralysis, and hemorrhaging, and in 1940 Paul Gyorgy identified biotin (vitamin H) as the cure.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000296.subject: choline
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000296.question: What does choline do in the body?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000296.answer_short: Choline is a structural building block of all cell membranes, plasma lipoproteins and lung surfactants, and part of the nervous system's sphingomyelin and acetylcholine.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000297.subject: choline
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000297.question: When was choline discovered?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000297.answer_short: Choline was first discovered and isolated from hog bile in 1862 and has been known in human and mammalian tissue ever since.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000298.subject: inositol
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000298.question: What is Inositol?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000298.answer_short: Inositol (myo-inositol) is a cyclic alcohol chemically similar to glucose that Wallach counts among the essential vitamins; in animals it is a major constituent of the phospholipids that build cell membranes.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000299.subject: inositol
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000299.question: How does inositol work in the body?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000299.answer_short: Myo-inositol triphosphate acts as a second messenger that mobilizes intracellular calcium in response to hormonal signals, and inositol is a building block of cell membranes.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000300.subject: inositol
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000300.question: Can you overdose on inositol?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000300.answer_short: Wallach reports that no signs of inositol overdose are known, even with large supplemental doses.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000301.subject: inositol
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000301.question: Does Wallach consider inositol a vitamin?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000301.answer_short: Yes — Wallach classifies inositol as one of the 16 essential vitamins for humans and non-human vertebrates.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000302.subject: flavonoids
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000302.question: What are flavonoids?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000302.answer_short: Flavonoids are biologically active plant pigments — the yellow, red, and blue colors in flowers — that come in three classes and that Wallach argues are essential nutrients.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000303.subject: flavonoids
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000303.question: How do flavonoids help the heart and cardiovascular system?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000303.answer_short: Wallach says flavonoids cut cardiovascular risk by reducing clotting, atherosclerosis, and blood pressure, easing oxidative and inflammatory stress on vessels, and improving endothelial function.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000304.subject: flavonoids
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000304.question: Are flavonoids essential nutrients?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000304.answer_short: Wallach says that although flavonoids aren't officially classed as essential, there is more than enough evidence to support a claim for their essentiality.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000305.subject: flavonoids
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000305.question: Why are flavonoids called that, and what is vitamin P?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000305.answer_short: The name comes from the Latin flavus (yellow); flavonoids were originally called vitamin P because they were related to the permeability levels of small blood vessels.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000324.subject: vitamin-k
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000324.question: Is vitamin K important for your bones?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000324.answer_short: Yes — Wallach says vitamin K is as essential to healthy bone maintenance as vitamin D, because the vitamin K-dependent protein osteocalcin directs calcium into bone.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000325.subject: vitamin-k
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000325.question: Do blood thinners like warfarin affect vitamin K?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000325.answer_short: Yes — Wallach says the coumarin blood thinners warfarin and dicumarol work by antagonizing (blocking) the action of vitamin K.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000326.subject: vitamin-k
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000326.question: Is vitamin K deficiency common?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000326.answer_short: No — Wallach says vitamin K deficiency is uncommon, except with a diet low in green leafy vegetables, antibiotic-suppressed gut flora, or a fat-absorption problem.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000327.subject: vitamin-k
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000327.question: How was vitamin K discovered?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000327.answer_short: In 1935 the researcher Dam observed a fatal bleeding disease in chicks on a complete diet that was cured when hog liver fat or alfalfa was added, revealing the missing clotting nutrient.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000328.subject: biotin
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000328.question: Can low biotin cause hair loss and gray hair?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000328.answer_short: Yes; biotin deficiency causes a progressive loss of both hair and hair color, along with skin lesions and nerve symptoms.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000329.subject: biotin
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000329.question: When was biotin discovered, and what else is it called?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000329.answer_short: Biotin - also called vitamin H or coenzyme R - was first isolated in 1936 and synthesized in 1943.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000330.subject: choline
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000330.question: What is choline?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000330.answer_short: Choline is an essential, vitamin-like nutrient the body cannot make in sufficient amounts on its own, needed to build cell membranes, carry fat out of the liver, and form the nerve-signal acetylcholine.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000331.subject: choline
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000331.question: What is choline?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000331.answer_short: Choline is an essential nutrient with a vitamin-like coenzyme function that has been recognized as essential for over a hundred years.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000332.subject: choline
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000332.question: Is choline a vitamin?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000332.answer_short: Wallach groups choline with the water-soluble vitamins, alongside the B-complex, biotin and vitamin C.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000333.subject: choline
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000333.question: How does choline help the brain and nerves?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000333.answer_short: Choline builds sphingomyelin in the brain and peripheral nerves and is the precursor for acetylcholine, so it is involved in transmitting nerve impulses.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000334.subject: choline
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000334.question: Does choline affect the liver?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000334.answer_short: Choline transports fat out of the liver, so a deficiency lets fat build up as a fatty liver that in severe cases can require a liver transplant.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000335.subject: choline
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000335.question: Can the body make its own choline?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000335.answer_short: The body can make some choline from methionine or serine with vitamin B12 and folate, but not enough to meet daily needs, so it must come from the diet.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000336.subject: choline
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000336.question: Can choline help tardive dyskinesia or Huntington's disease?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000336.answer_short: Wallach says large doses of choline have proved beneficial for managing and easing the symptoms of tardive dyskinesia and Huntington's disease in humans.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000337.subject: inositol
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000337.question: Where is inositol found in the body and why is it called muscle sugar?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000337.answer_short: Myoinositol, nicknamed "muscle sugar," resembles glucose and is concentrated in the brain, cerebrospinal fluid, muscle, heart, and especially the male reproductive organs and semen.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000338.subject: inositol
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000338.question: What foods are high in inositol?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000338.answer_short: Inositol occurs abundantly in whole grains and raw vegetables, present as inositol phospholipids and phytic acid.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000339.subject: inositol
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000339.question: Can inositol help diabetic neuropathy?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000339.answer_short: Wallach says inositol has been shown to have a therapeutic role in diabetic neuropathy.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000340.subject: flavonoids
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000340.question: How do flavonoids improve blood flow?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000340.answer_short: Wallach says flavanols in dark chocolate strengthen capillaries and boost nitric oxide, which relaxes blood-vessel muscle to lower blood pressure and improve blood flow.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000341.subject: flavonoids
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000341.question: Are flavonoids a vitamin?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000341.answer_short: Wallach says flavonoids — vitamin P, found in cocoa, tea, and wine — are now recognized as a third category of vitamins alongside the fat- and water-soluble groups.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000342.subject: flavonoids
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000342.question: Do the flavonoids in cocoa really prevent disease?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000342.answer_short: Wallach cites Harvard's Norman Hollenberg, who found the cocoa-drinking Kuna people have a 10% lower risk of four of the five most common killer diseases.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000343.subject: flavonoids
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000343.question: Who first discovered flavonoids and what were they first used to treat?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000343.answer_short: Flavonoids were first used clinically in 1936 by Szent-Gyorgyi to treat patients with capillary fragility and hemorrhages.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000512.subject: biotin
WAL-CLM-LETS-000512.question: What is the therapeutic dose of biotin compared to the RDA?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000512.answer_short: Wallach's Base Line program lists biotin at a 200 mcg RDA and true need, with a therapeutic (pharmacologic) daily dose of 500 to 3,000 mcg.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000076.subject: vitamin-k
WAL-CLM-LETS-000076.question: How much vitamin K should you take?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000076.answer_short: Wallach's Base Line Nutritional Supplement Program lists vitamin K at 140 mcg/day as his target (140 mcg is also the 30-day dose); the 70 mcg in the same row is the government RDA he prints only to argue against.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000034.subject: vitamin-k
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000034.question: What are the signs of vitamin K deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000034.answer_short: Vitamin K deficiency shows up as prolonged clotting time and abnormal bleeding — bruises, nosebleeds, blood in the urine and gut — plus bone problems like osteoporosis.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000240.subject: biotin
WAL-CLM-RARE-000240.question: What are the symptoms of a biotin deficiency?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000240.answer_short: Biotin deficiency causes eczema, alopecia (baldness), depression, hyperesthesia, paraesthesia, blepharitis, and gray or white hair.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000044.subject: choline
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000044.question: What are the signs of choline deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000044.answer_short: Choline deficiency can cause fatty liver, liver cirrhosis, kidney hemorrhage, Alzheimer's disease, dementia, tardive dyskinesia and Huntington's disease, with no known overdose.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000045.subject: inositol
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000045.question: What diseases does inositol deficiency cause?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000045.answer_short: Inositol deficiency can result in fat metabolism problems, fatty liver, diabetes, diabetic neuropathy, slow nerve conduction, and renal failure.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000052.subject: inositol
WAL-CLM-LETS-000052.question: How much inositol should I take daily?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000052.answer_short: Wallach's baseline supplement program lists a True Supplement Need of 90 mg of inositol daily, with a 30-day pharmacologic range of 500 to 2,000 mg.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000322.subject: inositol
WAL-CLM-LETS-000322.question: Can inositol help with insomnia and sleep?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000322.answer_short: Wallach includes inositol at 500 mg/day in his insomnia treatment protocol.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000012.subject: inositol
WAL-CLM-LETS-000012.question: Can inositol deficiency cause hair loss or eczema?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000012.answer_short: Wallach's deficiency chart lists alopecia (hair loss), constipation, eczema, and high cholesterol as signs of inositol deficiency.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000126.subject: flavonoids
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000126.question: How much bioflavonoids should I take per day?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000126.answer_short: Wallach's daily-supplement table in Epigenetics lists bioflavonoids at 1,000 to 5,000 mg per day.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000046.subject: flavonoids
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000046.question: What are the signs of a bioflavonoid deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000046.answer_short: Wallach lists capillary hemorrhage, easy bruising, nosebleeds, hemorrhoids, venous insufficiency, leg ulcers, weakened immunity, higher cancer risk, and a shortened lifespan.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000306.subject: flavonoids
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000306.question: What are flavonoids good for?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000306.answer_short: Wallach says flavonoid supplements reduce or eliminate allergies and inflammation, raise antioxidant activity, fight microbes, improve gut function, and support immunity in cancer patients.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000221.subject: vitamin-b3
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000221.question: Can niacin help with insomnia?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000221.answer_short: Wallach's insomnia protocol includes niacinamide at 1,000 mg at bedtime plus time-release niacin (B3) at 450 mg three times a day.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000222.subject: vanadium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000222.question: What is vanadium?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000222.answer_short: Vanadium is an essential trace mineral—proven essential in 1971—that works much like insulin to help the body control blood sugar.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000223.subject: vanadium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000223.question: What is vanadium?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000223.answer_short: Vanadium is an essential trace mineral, proven essential in 1971, that works like insulin to help control blood sugar.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000224.subject: vanadium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000224.question: What form of vanadium is best absorbed?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000224.answer_short: Plant-derived colloidal vanadium is absorbed at up to 98%, versus 40% for chelates and only 0.1-1% for metallic vanadyl sulfate.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000225.subject: vanadium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000225.question: How much vanadium should I take for low blood sugar?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000225.answer_short: Wallach calls chromium and vanadium the 'magic bullets' for hypoglycemia, at 50-200 mcg three times a day with meals.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000226.subject: vanadium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000226.question: What diseases does vanadium deficiency cause?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000226.answer_short: Wallach links vanadium deficiency to diabetes, hypoglycemia, high cholesterol and triglycerides, obesity, infertility, ADD/ADHD, depression, and bipolar disease.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000227.subject: germanium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000227.question: What is germanium?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000227.answer_short: Germanium is a trace mineral and metalloid element that Wallach counts among the body's essential nutrients; biologically it acts as a highly effective electrical impulse initiator inside cells and as a metallic cofactor for oxygen utilization.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000228.subject: germanium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000228.question: How does germanium work in the body?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000228.answer_short: In the body germanium acts as a highly effective intracellular electrical-impulse initiator and as a metallic cofactor for oxygen utilization.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000229.subject: germanium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000229.question: Does germanium boost the immune system?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000229.answer_short: Germanium enhances the immune system by stimulating natural killer cells, interferon, macrophages, and T-suppressor cells.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000230.subject: germanium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000230.question: What is GE-132 (organic germanium)?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000230.answer_short: GE-132, carboxyethyl germanium sesquioxide, is the organic form of germanium Asai synthesized in 1967; it is absorbed at about 30% efficiency and fully excreted within a week.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000231.subject: germanium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000231.question: Can germanium help prevent or fight cancer?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000231.answer_short: Germanium can be used for cancer prevention or therapy -- it raises oxygen flow into cells (cancer cells dislike oxygen) and stimulates immune cells and interferon.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000232.subject: germanium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000232.question: How is germanium used to treat Alzheimer's disease?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000232.answer_short: Wallach's Alzheimer's protocol includes germanium IM (5 ml of standard solution every other day for 24 days), then oral germanium at 150 mg twice a day.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000233.subject: germanium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000233.question: How was germanium's healing potential discovered?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000233.answer_short: In 1950 Japanese chemist Dr. Kazuhiko Asai found germanium in fossilized plant life and linked healing herbs to their high germanium levels, while Russian researchers tied it to anti-cancer activity.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000234.subject: manganese
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000234.question: Can manganese deficiency cause hearing loss in children?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000234.answer_short: Yes, in children a manganese and/or tin deficiency can cause reversible hearing loss.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000235.subject: manganese
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000235.question: How does Wallach treat carpal tunnel syndrome without surgery?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000235.answer_short: He treats it as a deficiency of arsenic, manganese, and choline, using B6, zinc, and plant-derived colloidal arsenic, manganese, and choline instead of wrist surgery.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000236.subject: manganese
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000236.question: Does Wallach use manganese for seizures or epilepsy?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000236.answer_short: Yes, manganese at 50 mg/day is part of his epilepsy protocol, alongside zinc, essential fatty acids, choline, taurine, and DMG.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000237.subject: manganese
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000237.question: Is carpal tunnel syndrome really caused by a mineral deficiency?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000237.answer_short: Wallach argues that repetitive motion injuries, and the millions of people wearing wrist, knee, and back supports, are all suffering from simple manganese deficiency.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000238.subject: boron
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000238.question: What does boron do in the body?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000238.answer_short: Boron supports bone metabolism, helps the body use calcium and magnesium efficiently, and is needed for proper function of the ovaries, testes, and adrenal glands.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000239.subject: cobalt
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000239.question: Why can vegans go years before a B12 deficiency shows up?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000239.answer_short: The body recycles B12 through an enterohepatic (gut-to-liver) circulation, so a deficiency in vegans may not appear for five to ten years after giving up meat.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000240.subject: lithium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000240.question: What does Wallach recommend for ADD and ADHD?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000240.answer_short: For ADD/ADHD, Wallach calls for removing all sugar and alcohol from the diet and taking plant-derived colloidal lithium, chromium and vanadium as specific supplements.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000241.subject: molybdenum
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000241.question: Can a molybdenum deficiency cause goiter?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000241.answer_short: Wallach lists molybdenum among the nutrient deficiencies that cause goiter, along with iodine, copper, and the amino acid tyrosine.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000307.subject: vanadium
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000307.question: Does vanadium fight cancer?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000307.answer_short: Wallach says vanadium has known anticarcinogenic properties and blocked mammary tumor growth in mice.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000308.subject: vanadium
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000308.question: Is type 2 diabetes really a mineral deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000308.answer_short: Wallach argues type 2 diabetes is not genetic but a simple deficiency of chromium and vanadium.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000309.subject: germanium
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000309.question: What foods and herbs contain germanium?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000309.answer_short: Beans and tuna carry small amounts, while healing herbs like garlic, ginseng, aloe, comfrey, chlorella and Shiitake mushroom concentrate germanium at 100 to 2,000 ppm.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000310.subject: germanium
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000310.question: Who discovered germanium and when?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000310.answer_short: Its existence was predicted by Mendeleev's periodic table, and the element was finally isolated in 1886 by a German chemist, Clemens Winkler, who named it germanium.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000311.subject: manganese
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000311.question: Can a mother's manganese deficiency make a baby deaf?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000311.answer_short: Yes, Wallach reports that infants born deaf are the result of mothers being deficient in manganese during pregnancy.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000312.subject: boron
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000312.question: Why is boron so rare?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000312.answer_short: Boron is produced by cosmic ray spallation rather than by stellar nucleosynthesis, making it a low-abundance element in both the solar system and Earth's crust.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000313.subject: boron
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000313.question: What is boric acid used for?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000313.answer_short: Boric acid has antiseptic, antifungal, and antiviral properties, and mild solutions are used as wound disinfectants and eye washes.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000314.subject: boron
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000314.question: Is boron used to treat cancer?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000314.answer_short: Yes, boron is the active ingredient in Bortezomib, a first-of-its-kind drug used to treat multiple myeloma and certain lymphomas.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000315.subject: boron
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000315.question: Is boron toxic or safe to take?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000315.answer_short: Borates have low toxicity in mammals, similar to table salt, but are more toxic to insects and so are used as insecticides.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000316.subject: boron
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000316.question: Is boron essential for all living things?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000316.answer_short: Yes, Wallach states that boron is essential to life for all organisms, including both plants and animals.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000317.subject: boron
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000317.question: What is the story behind 20 Mule Team Borax?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000317.answer_short: Large borax deposits were discovered in Death Valley in 1881, and the mined borax was hauled out by the famous 20-mule-team wagons.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000318.subject: boron
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000318.question: Where does the name boron come from?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000318.answer_short: The name 'boron' comes from the Arabic word 'buraq' and the Persian 'burah,' both names for borax.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000319.subject: cobalt
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000319.question: How was vitamin B12 discovered?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000319.answer_short: In 1948 two teams (in the UK and US) isolated pure B12, the anti-pernicious-anemia factor, gleaning just 20 mg from a ton of liver.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000055.subject: vanadium
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000055.question: Can low vanadium cause weight gain?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000055.answer_short: Without enough chromium and vanadium, blood glucose is converted into blood fats and body fat instead of being burned for energy.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000056.subject: manganese
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000056.question: What foods are high in manganese?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000056.answer_short: Hazelnuts (filberts) are a standout, with 24 nuts supplying ninety percent of the daily value for manganese.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000057.subject: molybdenum
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000057.question: Is molybdenum essential for plants?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000057.answer_short: Wallach lists molybdenum among the micronutrients that plants require for optimal health.

WAL-CLM-HELLS-000058.subject: molybdenum
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000058.question: Does molybdenum help prevent cancer?
WAL-CLM-HELLS-000058.answer_short: In a large China study Wallach cites, molybdenum had no statistically significant protective effect against cancer deaths, unlike beta carotene, vitamin E, and selenium.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000344.subject: vanadium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000344.question: What are the signs of a vanadium deficiency?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000344.answer_short: Wallach says carbohydrate and candy cravings, the 'munchies,' and a strong thirst for sweet drinks are sure signs of chromium and vanadium deficiency.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000345.subject: vanadium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000345.question: How did vanadium get its name?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000345.answer_short: Vanadium was named for the Scandinavian goddess Vanadis because of its many beautifully colored compounds.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000346.subject: germanium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000346.question: Is germanium used in electronics or computers?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000346.answer_short: Germanium is a poor conductor classed as a semiconductor, and when 'doped' with trace elements it is used to make transistors and microcomputers.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000347.subject: manganese
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000347.question: What does manganese do in the body?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000347.answer_short: Manganese activates many enzyme systems, including those for glucose metabolism, energy production, and the antioxidant SOD, and is built into metalloenzymes, hormones, and proteins.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000348.subject: manganese
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000348.question: Does manganese help build bones and cartilage?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000348.answer_short: Yes, manganese is essential to forming the three tiny bones of the ear and to the structure of joint cartilage.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000349.subject: manganese
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000349.question: Does manganese deficiency affect fertility and libido?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000349.answer_short: Yes, Wallach lists infertility (failure to ovulate, testicular atrophy), miscarriages, and loss of libido in both sexes among manganese-deficiency diseases.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000350.subject: manganese
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000350.question: Where does the name manganese come from?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000350.answer_short: Manganese was identified in 1774 by Carl Wilhelm Scheele, who named it from the Latin magnes ('magnet') for the magnetic properties of its ore.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000351.subject: boron
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000351.question: What is boron?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000351.answer_short: Boron is a scarce trace mineral Wallach counts among the nutrients essential for human health, needed for bone metabolism, the efficient use of calcium and magnesium, and normal sex-hormone levels.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000352.subject: boron
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000352.question: Where is boron found in nature?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000352.answer_short: Boron concentrates in plants, especially brown algae and land plants, at far higher levels than in animals.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000353.subject: boron
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000353.question: When was boron recognized as an essential nutrient?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000353.answer_short: Boron was not considered essential before 1981; it was first shown essential in growing chicks, and was not accepted as essential for humans until 1990.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000354.subject: boron
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000354.question: Who discovered boron?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000354.answer_short: Boron was first isolated in 1808 by English chemist Sir Humphry Davy together with French chemists Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac and Louis-Jacques Thenard.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000355.subject: cobalt
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000355.question: What is cobalt?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000355.answer_short: Cobalt is a rare trace mineral that's essential to all life — a single cobalt atom sits at the center of vitamin B12, so needing cobalt really means needing B12 (for blood, DNA, nerve myelin and thyroid hormone).

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000356.subject: cobalt
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000356.question: Why is vitamin B12 red?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000356.answer_short: B12's red color comes from the cobalt atom in the molecule, and about 30% of its activity is lost during cooking.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000357.subject: cobalt
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000357.question: What happens to extra vitamin B12 in the body?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000357.answer_short: The body stores a maximum of 2 mg of B12, releasing it slowly to the bone marrow; any excess is simply shed in the urine ('expensive urine').

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000358.subject: cobalt
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000358.question: Why do older people often need B12 shots?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000358.answer_short: Cobalt/B12 only absorbs when intrinsic factor is present and stomach pH is 2.0 or less; low stomach acid (often from too little salt) blocks it, so doctors give shots.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000359.subject: cobalt
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000359.question: Can you get too much cobalt?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000359.answer_short: Yes—cobalt excess of 20 to 30 mg a day can drive up red blood cell production by stimulating the kidney hormone erythropoietin.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000360.subject: cobalt
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000360.question: Can cobalt-poor soil cause deficiency in people?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000360.answer_short: Yes—less than 0.07 ppm cobalt in soil causes deficiency in the animals and people who eat crops from it, while 0.11 ppm prevents and cures it.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000361.subject: cobalt
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000361.question: How rare is cobalt and when was it discovered?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000361.answer_short: Cobalt is a rare element, only 0.003% of the earth's crust, and was first isolated as a metal by Swedish chemist Georg Brandt in 1739.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000362.subject: cobalt
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000362.question: Is cobalt magnetic and what is it used for?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000362.answer_short: Cobalt is easily magnetized and holds its magnetism at high temperatures; about a quarter of world production goes into 'alnico,' a super-magnetic alloy.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000363.subject: lithium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000363.question: What is lithium?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000363.answer_short: Lithium is the lightest of all metals and an essential trace mineral Wallach ties directly to mood and behavior — he treats depression, bipolar disorder, and aggression as hallmarks of a lithium deficiency.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000364.subject: lithium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000364.question: What kind of metal is lithium?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000364.answer_short: Lithium is an extremely reactive metal so light a small piece can float on water, and so reactive it must be stored in oil or kerosene.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000365.subject: lithium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000365.question: Why is lithium used to treat bipolar disorder?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000365.answer_short: Lithium carbonate is routinely prescribed for severe bipolar disorder — over 3 million prescriptions a year — with its effect thought to involve how brain cells respond to certain hormones and neurotransmitters.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000366.subject: lithium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000366.question: Is depression caused by a lithium deficiency?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000366.answer_short: Wallach holds that depression and manic depression are simply a lithium deficiency aggravated by high sugar consumption.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000367.subject: lithium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000367.question: How did lithium get its name?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000367.answer_short: Lithium was discovered in 1817 by Swedish chemist Johan August Arfvedson and named after the Greek word 'lithos,' meaning 'stone.'

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000368.subject: molybdenum
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000368.question: What is molybdenum?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000368.answer_short: Molybdenum is an essential trace mineral in Wallach's framework — a hard, silvery metal mined from the ore molybdenite — that every living organism needs as a building block of several key enzymes.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000369.subject: molybdenum
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000369.question: Can you take too much molybdenum? Is it toxic?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000369.answer_short: Wallach says molybdenum toxicity occurs at 10 mg per day, showing up as a gout-like disease and as interference with copper metabolism.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000370.subject: molybdenum
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000370.question: Can too much molybdenum in soil poison animals?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000370.answer_short: Wallach says a few soils worldwide are rich enough in molybdenum to poison animals grazing on the plants, while numerous other soils are molybdenum-deficient.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000371.subject: molybdenum
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000371.question: Who discovered molybdenum and when?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000371.answer_short: Molybdenum was first extracted from molybdenite and identified as a new element in 1778 by a Swedish chemist named Scheele.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000513.subject: vanadium
WAL-CLM-LETS-000513.question: Are diabetes and hypoglycemia really caused by vanadium deficiency?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000513.answer_short: Wallach says diabetes and hypoglycemia are, in reality, deficiencies of chromium and vanadium created by malabsorption from celiac-type intestinal changes.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000358.subject: vanadium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000358.question: Was vanadium once considered toxic?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000358.answer_short: Wallach says vanadium was among soil elements once deemed totally toxic with no possibility of being essential, and that doctors made sure it stayed out of our food.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000359.subject: vanadium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000359.question: Is vanadium found in living creatures?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000359.answer_short: Wallach notes that a vanadium respiratory compound was found in the blood of sea squirts, among the early discoveries of trace minerals in animals.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000360.subject: manganese
WAL-CLM-RARE-000360.question: What is manganese?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000360.answer_short: Manganese is an essential trace mineral — the body holds only 10 to 20 mg in all — that activates key enzymes and helps build bones, joint cartilage, and the tiny bones of the ear.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000361.subject: manganese
WAL-CLM-RARE-000361.question: How was manganese used as a medicine historically?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000361.answer_short: In the 1800s manganese cured miners' scabies dermatitis, treated certain anemias better than iron, and was used for menstrual disorders like amenorrhea.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000362.subject: boron
WAL-CLM-RARE-000362.question: How is boron used to treat brain tumors?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000362.answer_short: Boron neutron capture therapy combines a boron-containing drug with neutron irradiation of the brain to treat brain tumors.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000363.subject: cobalt
WAL-CLM-RARE-000363.question: What foods are a good source of cobalt?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000363.answer_short: Organ meats like liver and kidney significantly boost the availability of cobalt, along with selenium, sulfur, molybdenum and zinc.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000364.subject: lithium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000364.question: What was lithium used to treat before modern medicine?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000364.answer_short: Lithium's medicinal use goes back to 400 AD for mental illness, and in the 1840s lithium salts were used to treat kidney stones, gout and rheumatism.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000365.subject: lithium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000365.question: Is lithium an essential nutrient?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000365.answer_short: Yes — Wallach counts lithium among the trace elements whose essentiality was established in mice in the late 20th century.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000366.subject: molybdenum
WAL-CLM-RARE-000366.question: Was molybdenum once considered toxic or non-essential?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000366.answer_short: Yes - Wallach says molybdenum was one of dozens of soil elements the medical profession recently dismissed as totally toxic with no possibility of being essential.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000081.subject: vanadium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000081.question: Does hair analysis show a vanadium deficiency?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000081.answer_short: Wallach says the diabetes/hypoglycemia hair-analysis pattern shows low chromium, vanadium, sodium, potassium, manganese, and zinc.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000256.subject: vanadium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000256.question: Does vanadium lower cholesterol?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000256.answer_short: Wallach says vanadium inhibits cholesterol synthesis, lowering blood cholesterol and cholesterol in the aorta.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000138.subject: vanadium
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000138.question: What is the recommended daily dose of vanadium?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000138.answer_short: Wallach's Epigenetics mineral table lists vanadium at 50-100 mcg per 100 pounds of body weight for adults and children.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000035.subject: vanadium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000035.question: Can vanadium help with diabetes and low blood sugar?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000035.answer_short: Wallach says vanadium acts like insulin—making cell receptors more sensitive—and could reduce or even eliminate most adult-onset diabetes.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000047.subject: vanadium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000047.question: Can vanadium replace insulin for diabetes?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000047.answer_short: Wallach cites a medical school's finding that vanadium will replace insulin for adult-onset diabetics.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000086.subject: germanium
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000086.question: What are the signs of germanium deficiency?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000086.answer_short: Germanium deficiency is typified by a severely reduced immune status, arthritis, osteoarthritis, low energy, and cancer.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000011.subject: germanium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000011.question: How much germanium should I take a day?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000011.answer_short: The recommended maintenance dose is 20 to 30 mg per day; 50 to 100 mg per day is common when serious illness calls for higher oxygen levels in the body.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000134.subject: manganese
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000134.question: How much manganese should I take each day?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000134.answer_short: In Wallach's Base Line Nutritional Supplement Program the True Supplement Need for manganese is 5 mg a day (vs. the 2.5 mg government RDA), with a 30-day pharmacologic dose range of 2 to 50 mg.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000175.subject: manganese
WAL-CLM-RARE-000175.question: Can too much manganese be harmful?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000175.answer_short: Yes, excessive manganese from water supplies or industry can cause a Parkinson-like syndrome or a schizophrenia-like disorder called locura manganica.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000017.subject: manganese
WAL-CLM-LETS-000017.question: What are the signs of manganese deficiency and manganese toxicity?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000017.answer_short: Deficiency brings ataxia, atherosclerosis, dizziness, hearing loss, high cholesterol, low blood sugar, and tinnitus; toxicity brings anorexia, impaired judgment, Parkinsonism, and memory loss.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000026.subject: manganese
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000026.question: What diseases does manganese deficiency cause?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000026.answer_short: Wallach calls manganese deficiency striking, causing birth defects like congenital ataxia and deafness, plus asthma, convulsions, stunted growth, skeletal defects, and joint disorders like TMJ and carpal tunnel.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000043.subject: boron
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000043.question: Does boron raise testosterone and estrogen?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000043.answer_short: Wallach reports that boron supplementation doubles blood levels of both estrogen (estradiol) and testosterone in men and women.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000079.subject: cobalt
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000079.question: What does cobalt do in the body?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000079.answer_short: Cobalt is essential for all forms of life; it activates enzymes, helps fix nitrogen, and sits at the very center of vitamin B12.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000084.subject: cobalt
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000084.question: How much cobalt or vitamin B12 should I take a day?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000084.answer_short: The RDA is only 3–4 mcg a day, but Wallach prefers 250 to 400 mcg for a real safety margin, especially before and during pregnancy and nursing.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000083.subject: cobalt
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000083.question: What diseases does a cobalt or vitamin B12 deficiency cause?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000083.answer_short: Failing to absorb B12/cobalt causes pernicious anemia and demyelination of the spinal cord and large nerve trunks.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000082.subject: cobalt
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000082.question: How was cobalt discovered to be essential?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000082.answer_short: It came from 'bush sickness,' a fatal wasting disease of cattle and sheep in Australia and New Zealand that was cured and prevented by cobalt.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000200.subject: lithium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000200.question: What are the signs of a lithium deficiency?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000200.answer_short: In animals lithium deficiency causes reproductive failure, infertility, poor growth and shortened life; in humans it shows as manic depression, rages, hyperactivity, ADD/ADHD, some autism and 'bad seed' behavior.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000202.subject: lithium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000202.question: Do violent criminals have low lithium levels?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000202.answer_short: Wallach reports that normal controls have almost 400 times more hair lithium than violent criminals from California, Florida, Texas and Oregon.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000199.subject: lithium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000199.question: How much lithium should you take and in what form?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000199.answer_short: Wallach cites chelated lithium at 1,000 to 2,000 micrograms per day, which raises hair lithium levels over weeks — unlike metallic lithium carbonate.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000167.subject: lithium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000167.question: Does taking lithium affect vitamin B12 or other minerals?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000167.answer_short: Wallach notes that short-term lithium supplementation raises serum vitamin B12 but long-term use lowers it, while raising the hair concentrations of vanadium, aluminum, lead, arsenic and cobalt.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000029.subject: lithium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000029.question: Does Wallach want lithium added to drinking water?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000029.answer_short: Yes -- Wallach wants lithium added to the public water supply and fluoride eliminated; conventional medicine limits lithium to psychiatric use, especially manic depression.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000041.subject: lithium
WAL-CLM-RARE-000041.question: Is there a link between lithium in drinking water and crime rates?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000041.answer_short: Wallach cites a University of California, San Diego study relating violent crime in 27 Texas counties (1978-1987) to drinking-water lithium, finding significantly higher rates of suicide, homicide and rape in counties with little or no lithium.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000100.subject: molybdenum
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000100.question: What does molybdenum do in the body?
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000100.answer_short: Molybdenum is essential to all organisms as part of metalloenzymes and is an integral part of at least three enzymes: xanthine oxidase, aldehyde oxidase, and sulfite oxidase.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000180.subject: molybdenum
WAL-CLM-RARE-000180.question: What is the RDA for molybdenum and how much do people usually get?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000180.answer_short: Wallach cites an RDA for molybdenum of 250 mcg per day, with average American dietary intake ranging from 76 to 109 mcg per day.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000058.subject: molybdenum
WAL-CLM-LETS-000058.question: How much molybdenum should I take as a supplement?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000058.answer_short: Wallach's Base Line Nutritional Supplement Program for adults lists molybdenum at a true supplement need of 500 mcg per day, versus an RDA of only 15 mcg, with a pharmacologic daily dose of 1,000 mcg.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000242.subject: sodium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000242.question: What is Addison's disease and why does it cause salt cravings?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000242.answer_short: Addison's disease is failure of the adrenal cortex; Wallach says it causes the body to lose sodium and produces a marked 'salt hunger' relieved by salt.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000243.subject: sodium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000243.question: Does craving salt mean something is wrong?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000243.answer_short: Wallach says craving salt is a form of pica — a symptom caused only by one or more mineral deficiencies.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000244.subject: sodium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000244.question: Can not getting enough salt actually kill you?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000244.answer_short: Yes — Wallach blames the 1993 US heat wave deaths on simple salt deficiency, noting almost all who died were on salt-restricted diets.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000245.subject: sodium
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000245.question: Should pregnant women go on a low-salt diet?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000245.answer_short: No — Wallach says pregnancy toxemia (eclampsia) is the result of the low-protein, low-salt diets some women adopt to limit weight gain in pregnancy, not something salt restriction prevents.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000246.subject: phosphorus
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000246.question: What is phosphorus?
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000246.answer_short: Phosphorus is an extremely important essential mineral that Wallach says has more functions in the body than any other mineral, yet nutritionists ignore it because it is in nearly all foods.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000247.subject: phosphorus
